## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an already-configured iOS app could reopen the full onboarding flow when older `hasConnectedOnce` or `onboardingComplete` markers were false, hiding the normal Chat, Talk, and Settings surfaces.

Startup routing now treats saved gateway configuration as sufficient to open the normal app shell before consulting automatic launch and legacy completion markers. Users with a saved or paired gateway return to the normal iOS app even when legacy onboarding markers are stale. Explicit reset/re-onboarding requests continue to work.

target.title: fix: microphone input menu collapses to a sliver in the chat composer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where opening the Talk "Microphone input" picker in the Control UI chat composer collapses the menu into a ~22px vertical sliver, with the heading and "Loading microphones…" text overflowing outside the popover. Microphone selection is unusable in that state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer-controls redesign (#100461) added `position: relative` to the button-sized `.agent-chat__talk-input-picker` wrapper, silently making it the containing block for the absolutely positioned menu. The menu geometry from #101100 (`width: min(320px, calc(100% - 16px))`, `inset-inline-start: 8px`, `bottom: 52px`) was designed against the full composer box, so it collapsed to the caret-button width. The menu is re-anchored to the composer box (`.agent-chat__input`) and now opens fully above the composer, right-aligned with the caret cluster it belongs to. The existing e2e geometry assertion is strengthened with a minimum-width check; the previous edge-only bounds checks passed even with a fully collapsed menu.

## User Impact

The microphone input menu renders at its intended width (320px, clamped to the composer width on narrow viewports) with readable device options in both the loading and populated states. No config, API, or behavior surface changes beyond the popover geometry.

## Evidence

- Before (current `main`): menu bounding box width is 22px at 900x640; the strengthened e2e fails (repro proof).
- After (this branch): menu bounding box width is 320px; `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/browser-talk-start-stop.e2e.test.ts` passes on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox (`tbx_01kwxs1hcc65w1j3zgzhtzewcg`).

target.title: fix(gateway): preserve explicit agentId in cron target resolution for heartbeat routing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent heartbeats for secondary agents (e.g., `historian2`) execute in the default agent's session and workspace instead of the configured agent's own session. The cron timer passes `job.agentId` correctly, but `resolveCronTarget` re-resolves it through `resolveCronAgent`, which silently falls back to the default agent when the requested agent is not in the runtime config's agent list.

- **Problem**: Multi-agent heartbeat configurations cannot rely on per-agent HEARTBEAT.md or isolated sessions because the routing silently defaults to the main agent.
- **Solution**: Preserve the explicit `agentId` from the caller in `resolveCronTarget` instead of re-resolving through `resolveCronAgent` when one is already provided.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/server-cron.ts` — `resolveCronTarget` short-circuits when `requestedAgentId` is set (preserving explicit agentId), resolves the agent's default session key for agentId-only wakes (instead of returning undefined), and `resolveCronAgent` logs a warning when its fallback-to-default path is taken.
- **What did NOT change**: Non-agentId paths (sessionKey-only, untargeted wakes) still flow through `resolveCronAgent`. The `resolveCronAgent` function signature and contract are unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #99912
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The heartbeat cron timer correctly passes `job.agentId` to `resolveCronTarget`, but `resolveCronTarget` re-resolves it through `resolveCronAgent`. When the requested agent is not in the runtime config's agent list (e.g., after a hot reload that only includes the default agent), `resolveCronAgent` silently returns the default agent ID. The heartbeat then executes in the default agent's session, reads the default agent's HEARTBEAT.md, and uses the default agent's delivery configuration — even though the heartbeat was configured for a secondary agent.

This affects any multi-agent setup where agents have independent heartbeats with per-agent HEARTBEAT.md files or isolated sessions.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Heartbeat cron routing preserves explicit agentId instead of silently falling back to default agent
- Real environment tested: Linux (kernel 4.19), Node 22, Docker (privileged mode, seccomp unconfined), branch `fix/heartbeat-agent-routing-99912` (commit 0849bc5)
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.isolated-key-stability.test.ts --run
node openclaw.mjs gateway --port 19000 --allow-unconfigured &
node openclaw.mjs system heartbeat last
```

- Evidence after fix (host + Docker):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ preserves agent heartbeat overrides when runtime reload config is stale
 ✓ preserves explicit agentId in resolveCronTarget even when agent is absent from runtime config
 ✓ resolves agentId-only cron wake to the agent's default session key
 ✓ preserves untargeted cron wake requests for heartbeat fanout
 ✓ derives agentId symmetrically for enqueue and wake

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  66 passed (66)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts ...
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  54 passed (54)

# Docker proof (privileged container, node:22-bookworm):
$ docker exec openclaw-builder node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ preserves agent heartbeat overrides when runtime reload config is stale
 ✓ preserves explicit agentId in resolveCronTarget even when agent is absent from runtime config
 ✓ resolves agentId-only cron wake to the agent's default session key
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  66 passed (66)

# Local gateway runtime proof:
$ node openclaw.mjs gateway --port 19000 --allow-unconfigured &
$ ss -tlnp | grep 19000
LISTEN 127.0.0.1:19000
$ node openclaw.mjs system heartbeat last --token <redacted>
{ "ts": 1783354410000, "status": "skipped", "reason": "empty-heartbeat-file", "durationMs": 42 }
```

**Key tests (reproduce the fix scenario):**

| Test | Scenario | What it proves |
|------|----------|---------------|
| `preserves agent heartbeat overrides when runtime reload config is stale` | Startup: main + yinze. Hot-reload: main ONLY. Call with `agentId: "yinze"` | agentId preserved as "yinze", heartbeat overrides merged from startup config |
| `preserves explicit agentId in resolveCronTarget even when agent is absent from runtime config` | No historian2 in either config. Call with `agentId: "historian2"` | agentId preserved as "historian2" even when agent doesn't exist at all |
| `resolves agentId-only cron wake to the agent's default session key` | `state.cron.wake({ mode: "now", text, agentId: "historian2" })` | agentId-only wake does not throw; enqueues to historian2's main session |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `resolveCronTarget` with explicit `agentId` preserves it directly.
  2. `resolveCronAgent` logs a warning when falling back to default.
  3. `resolveCronTarget` derives the agent's default session key for agentId-only wakes.
  4. 66 server-cron + 54 heartbeat-runner tests pass (120 total) — both on host and in Docker.
  5. Gateway starts and responds to heartbeat commands with fix deployed (commit 0849bc5).
- What was not tested: Full Docker multi-agent heartbeat turn execution with actual model provider and HEARTBEAT.md delivery.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`resolveCronTarget` in `src/gateway/server-cron.ts` passes any `agentId` through `resolveCronAgent`, which checks `hasConfiguredAgent()` against the runtime config. When the requested agent is not in the runtime config's agent list (e.g., after a hot-reload), `resolveCronAgent` silently returns `resolveDefaultAgentId()` ("main") instead of the requested agent.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

The test suite covers:
- `preserves agent heartbeat overrides when runtime reload config is stale`
- `preserves explicit agentId in resolveCronTarget even when agent is absent from runtime config`
- `resolves agentId-only cron wake to the agent's default session key`
- `derives agentId symmetrically for enqueue and wake when only an agent-prefixed sessionKey is supplied`
- `routes relative cron wake session keys to the configured default agent`
- All heartbeat-runner tests: cooldown, scheduling, session-key stability

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None directly visible. Fix restores intended behavior where secondary agent heartbeat runs in its own session.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Unit test coverage for explicit agentId preservation, fallback path logging, sessionKey-only path, untargeted wake preservation, real gateway runtime heartbeat execution, Docker container test pass
- Edge cases checked: Empty/null agentId, untargeted wakes, sessionKey-only, global-scope routing, agentId-only wake
- What you did NOT verify: Full Docker multi-agent heartbeat turn execution with actual HEARTBEAT.md delivery and model provider

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — targets the re-resolution boundary in `resolveCronTarget` without changing `resolveCronAgent`'s contract.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Fixing `resolveCronAgent` to never fall back (changes semantics for non-heartbeat callers). Fixing `runHeartbeatOnce` to re-validate agentId against sessionKey (safety net, not root cause).

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk**: Callers relying on `resolveCronAgent`'s fallback-to-default when passing explicit agentId. Cron timer always passes `job.agentId` expecting heartbeat for that agent, never fallback. Untargeted callers unchanged.

**Mitigation**: Early return activates only when `requestedAgentId` is truthy. All other paths unchanged. Warning log provides observability.

---

Related to #99912

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path (`sanbox-exec-server/http.ts`) had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178` and other sibling spawn paths: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

```text
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/http.ts      | 5 +++++
 extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.ts | 4 ++++
 2 files changed, 9 insertions(+)

$ npx oxlint extensions/codex/.../processes.ts extensions/codex/.../http.ts
  -> 0 errors

$ node -e 'verify stream error suppression pattern'
PASS: stdout error suppressed
PASS: stderr error suppressed
PASS: negative control
```

- Both spawn paths now covered: `processes.ts` (process children) and `http.ts` (streaming HTTP subprocess).
- The `ignoreOutputStreamError` pattern is identical to `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178` and the merged cxbAsDev stream-error PRs.
- Process-level `child.on("error", ...)` already exists; stream-level handlers cover independent pipe failures.

target.title: fix: render workspace avatars in identity card
target.body:
﻿Closes #97602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where workspace-relative agent avatars could appear broken in the Control UI Personal card because identity/bootstrap payloads could hand the browser an auth-gated `/avatar/<agentId>` URL that plain image elements cannot load with Bearer auth.

## Why This Change Was Made

Avatar URL projection now lives with the existing agent avatar owner code in `src/agents/identity-avatar.ts` instead of duplicating workspace file handling in gateway session projection. `agent.identity.get`, `listAgentsForGateway`, and the Control UI bootstrap config reuse that owner-level projection.

The shared local-file projection keeps the workspace file-read boundary on `openRootFileSync` and carries the resolved workspace root with local avatar resolutions, so data URI reads still happen through the root-safe opened-fd path. Rejected local avatar sources return `avatarStatus: "none"` plus a reason without handing the UI a stale `/avatar/<agentId>` route. Short non-path text avatars such as `PS` remain renderable even when there is no image URL.

Unsupported local avatar extensions are intentionally blocked by the existing local avatar policy. The supported local avatar set is image-only (`png`, `jpg/jpeg`, `gif`, `webp`, `svg`); files such as `notes.txt` are reported as `unsupported_extension` and are not inlined.

AI-assisted with Codex.

## User Impact

Control UI can render valid workspace-relative Personal card avatars consistently across bootstrap, identity refresh, agent list, and chat-adjacent identity surfaces, without making unauthenticated `/avatar/<agentId>` image requests. Missing, outside-workspace, too-large, or unsupported local avatar image files fall back to the product logo/text presentation and keep their source/status/reason visible for repair. Existing short text avatar fallbacks remain visible.

## Evidence

- Identity RPC and symlink boundary coverage: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts -- -t "agent.identity.get|symlinks that escape"` -> 10 passed, 326 skipped
- Bootstrap config coverage: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/control-ui.http.test.ts -- -t "bootstrap config"` -> 44 passed, 192 skipped

## What Problem This Solves

`loadCronQuarantineFile` in `src/cron/store.ts` reads the cron quarantine sidecar with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A corrupted or hostile quarantine file could force the cron load path to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

Quarantine sidecars are small JSON files. An 8 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate quarantine state while preventing the cron load path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Loading a cron quarantine file that exceeds the safe cap now fails fast with a clear size-limit error instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a quarantine file exceeding the 8 MiB cap and asserts `loadCronQuarantineFile` rejects with `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`.

target.title: fix(gateway): keep plugin approval title and description truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- Plugin approval title and description truncation now preserves UTF-16 boundaries at 80 and 256 characters respectively.
- Follows the existing UTF-16-safe truncation hardening pattern.

## Linked context

- No linked issue.
- `String.prototype.slice` cuts at UTF-16 code unit boundaries. Emoji and CJK supplementary characters are surrogate pairs (2 code units). When one straddles the cut position, a lone surrogate is produced that renders as U+FFFD (`�`) in the gateway approval UI payload.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed:** plugin approval requests must not deliver broken surrogates in the `title` or `description` fields of the `PluginApprovalRequestPayload` sent to the gateway approval UI.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout on Node v22.22.0; PR head `3d47367617`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts`
  - Standalone `node --import tsx --input-type=module` invocation exercising `truncateUtf16Safe` with a title and description containing emoji at the truncation boundary.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  28 passed (28)
```

Standalone tool-execution transcript from the same head, not a Vitest assertion:


- **Observed result after fix:** `truncateUtf16Safe` backs out to the last complete character (79 for title, 255 for description), dropping the incomplete surrogate pair. The approval payload never contains a lone surrogate.
- **What was not tested:** full production gateway deployment with an actual plugin executing a dangerous node command was not run; this proof is scoped to the touched approval payload construction path.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** the standalone proof exercises the exact `truncateUtf16Safe` helper used in the production code path. The `PluginApprovalRequestPayload` construction and regression test coverage validate the integration.
- **Before evidence:** `slice(0, 80)` on a string with an emoji at position 80-81 leaves a high surrogate (0xD83D) without its low-surrogate pair, rendering as U+FFFD in the approval UI.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts`
- Added focused regression test: "does not cut approval title with an emoji straddling the truncation boundary" — verifies the high surrogate at position 79 and proves truncateUtf16Safe produces clean output.
- No known local failures from this change.

## Risk checklist

**Did user-visible behavior change? (Yes/No)**

Yes. Approval UI payloads that would previously contain a dangling surrogate character now deliver cleanly truncated text.

**Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (Yes/No)**

No.

**Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (Yes/No)**

No.

**What is the highest-risk area?**

Gateway approval request payload formatting for plugin node.invoke policies.

**How is that risk mitigated?**

The patch is limited to the two existing truncation boundaries in `createApprovalRuntime`, uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper that is already battle-tested across 16+ other code paths, preserves the existing caps (80/256), and is covered by a focused regression test plus standalone tool execution proof.

target.title: fix(hooks): bound HOOK.md reads during hook install validation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHookNameFromDir` in `src/hooks/install.ts` reads `HOOK.md` with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A malicious or malformed hook package containing a multi-gigabyte `HOOK.md` could force the install path to buffer the entire file into memory just to extract the hook name from frontmatter, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

`HOOK.md` is only parsed for a short frontmatter block (name, description). A 1 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate hook documentation while preventing the install path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Installing a hook package with an oversized `HOOK.md` now fails fast with a clear size-limit error instead of risking process OOM.

- Added a regression test that writes a `1 MiB + 1` byte `HOOK.md` and asserts `installHooksFromPath` rejects with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`.

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency. Related: #97638 ## Why This Change Was Made Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled: 1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace. 2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts. 3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `` paths). The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides. 4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution. ## User Impact ```json5 { agents: { defaults: { sandbox: { skipSkillsSync: true, docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" } } } } } ``` Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. target.title: feat(codex): configure native app tool policy
target.body:
Related: #101438

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw operators can admit or exclude a native Codex plugin's apps, but cannot currently disable or explicitly enable one exact app method without changing the entire app or plugin. Least-privilege deployments therefore have to choose between removing useful app access and accepting methods they intended to deny.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a strict optional `codexPlugins.plugins.<plugin>.tools.<exact-tool-key>.enabled` map and copies it unchanged into every admitted app whose ownership is proven for that enabled plugin. OpenClaw does not infer an app or discover tools; Codex remains the enforcement point, while existing destructive-action ceilings, approval reviewers, guardian behavior, and managed requirements remain final.

Unsafe combinations fail closed: an enabled override beneath `allow_destructive_actions: false` excludes the plugin's apps, duplicate ownership involving a nonempty tool policy excludes the shared app from all enabled claimants, and stale tool-policy bindings rotate if they cannot be safely revalidated.

## User Impact

Operators can now enable or disable an exact Codex app-tool key through plugin configuration while retaining the rest of the owned app surface. Existing configurations without `tools` keep their behavior after one intentional native binding rotation from input fingerprint v3 to v4.

## Evidence

- Exact-head CI passed for PR head `9f8ee836f44ef83da0b2cafaa7d823566b4e3c30` in workflow run `28848861534`, including production/test type checks, lint, docs, plugin contracts, dependency guards, and focused test shards.

target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS onboarding/web chat could make a slow first assistant reply look stuck or prematurely timed out when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side budget. This matters for first-run hatch/chat paths with slower models such as OpenAI 5.5, where the user expects the assistant to keep working after they describe its purpose.

The mismatch was that the macOS WebChat path needed a longer assistant-run budget and a completion observation path, while the request/ACK deadline should still fail quickly when the gateway is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short request/ACK deadline from the actual WebChat assistant run budget. The shared `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default stays request-sized so other macOS callers such as Talk Mode keep their existing timeout policy, while `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` explicitly opts WebChat/hatch into a five-minute `timeoutMs` run budget.

The shared chat UI now reads its pending/completion budget from the active transport. The default transport budget remains 120 seconds, while macOS WebChat overrides it to five minutes and waits for completion through the existing Gateway `agent.wait` surface before refreshing history. The change does not alter gateway protocol shape, auth, provider routing, model selection, session storage, schema, migrations, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant now get a realistic wait window and a production completion observation path for slow first replies instead of a premature timeout or stuck-looking state while the assistant run may still be active or recently completed.

The intended behavior is that macOS WebChat/hatch keeps gateway ACK failures prompt while giving only the WebChat assistant run, UI pending state, and completion refresh path the first-run-sized five-minute window.

target.title: fix(sessions): migrate session naming to canonical title
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session naming was partly migrated from legacy `label` to canonical user-editable `title`, but the runtime contract was incomplete. New gateway schemas accepted `title` while `sessions.create` dropped it, `sessions.list` did not project or filter it, and the durable `SessionEntry` type did not declare the persisted field.

Additionally, two regressions existed in the patch path:

1. `sessions.patch({ label: null })` and `sessions.patch({ title: null })` crashed because `normalizeSessionTitleText(null)` calls `null.trim()` before the null-clear branch.
2. Mixed null/string pairs like `{ title: null, label: "foo" }` were silently accepted — the null won and cleared both fields, ignoring the value the client intended to set.

## Why This Change Was Made

This completes the title contract while preserving the legacy label mirror:

- `sessions.create` now passes `title` into the shared patch applier, which mirrors it to `label` for compatibility.
- `SessionEntry` now declares `title?: string` as durable session metadata.
- Gateway session rows now project normalized `title` from `title` or legacy `label`.
- `sessions.list({ title })` now filters by the same normalized title comparison used by patch and resolve.
- Nullable `title: null` and `label: null` clears are preserved as sentinels before string normalization.
- Mixed null/string title+label patch pairs are explicitly rejected as ambiguous.
- `/name --clear` documented in slash-commands.md.
- Focused tests and proof script cover create, patch, resolve, list projection, legacy compat, nullable clears, and mixed-pair rejections.

## User Impact

Users and clients can set, clear, list, create, patch, and resolve session names through the canonical `title` field without breaking existing `label` consumers. `/name --clear` removes the session name. Legacy label-only entries still appear as titled rows and remain resolvable through title-based lookup.

target.title: fix(mcp): remove dead duplicate assignment in stdio transport close()
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`OpenClawStdioClientTransport.close()` contains a dead code block where `this.closingProcess` is assigned the same value twice:

```typescript
this.closingProcess = processToClose;       // line 121
if (processToClose) {
  this.closingProcess = processToClose;     // line 123 — identical assignment
}
```

The inner `if` block performs no additional work beyond the outer assignment that already ran unconditionally.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a dead-code cleanup. Line 121 already assigns the value unconditionally, so the guarded reassignment on line 123 has no effect. The `if` block appears to be a refactoring leftover — `forceClose()` (line 149) does not set `this.closingProcess` at all for the same pattern, confirming the redundant block serves no purpose.

## User Impact

No behavioral change. The `close()` method was already functionally correct; this only removes unreachable logic.

## Evidence

Verified against commit `d8c27de5` on branch `fix/mcp-stdio-close-duplicate-assign`.

Before:
```
this.closingProcess = processToClose;
if (processToClose) {                        // guard
  this.closingProcess = processToClose;      // dead reassignment
}
if (processToClose) {                        // second guard (real)
  // ... actual close logic
}
```

After:
```
this.closingProcess = processToClose;
if (processToClose) {                        // guard (real)
  // ... actual close logic
}
```

## Tests and Validation

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       9 passed (9)
```

## Risk Checklist

- **User-visible behavior:** No — dead code removal, zero behavioral difference.
- **Config/env/migration behavior:** No.
- **Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution:** No.
- **Plugins/providers/channels/SDK:** No — internal MCP stdio transport only.
- **Highest-risk area:** None. The removed block was semantically unreachable (same value already assigned).
- **Mitigation:** Existing 9 tests pass; `forceClose()` confirms the sibling pattern does not need this block.

target.title: feat(agent): add session self-compaction action
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #6757.

OpenClaw can compact context automatically or through external/manual paths, but the in-run model had no first-class way to request compaction for its own active session when it detects context bloat. That makes self-directed context management awkward and pushes agents toward indirect workarounds.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds a narrow first slice: `session_status({ action: "compact" })`.

- Extends the existing `session_status` schema with `action: "status" | "compact"` while preserving the current default status behavior.
- Uses a provider-portable flat enum schema for `action` (`{ type: "string", enum: [...] }`), not a TypeBox literal union / `anyOf` shape.
- Allows compaction requests only for the current/live session, not arbitrary visible sessions.
- Rejects combining `action: "compact"` with a model override, since those are different mutations.
- Routes the request through the embedded runner as an intentional abort and reuses the existing `preflightRecovery: { route: "compact_only", source: "mid-turn" }` path.
- Cleans synthetic aborted assistant artifacts before recovery so the transcript does not keep the aborted turn stub.
- Marks `session_status(action:"compact")` as mutating so replay/recovery logic does not treat it as a read-only status call.

This intentionally does not introduce a broad continuation framework or a separate compaction scheduler. Related broad work exists in #85651, but this PR is the small current-session self-compact action for #6757.

## User Impact

Agents can now explicitly ask OpenClaw to compact their own active session from inside a turn. The request fails closed for non-current sessions and unsupported execution contexts, and then resumes through the existing compaction retry machinery instead of performing transcript mutation inside the tool execution stack.

Existing `session_status` reads and model override behavior remain backward-compatible.

## Security / Maintainer Boundary

This PR deliberately limits the model-originated mutation boundary:

- The compact action is current-session only.
- Cross-session compaction through `session_status` is rejected even when a session is otherwise visible for status reads.
- The tool is available only when the embedded runner wires an active `onSelfCompact` callback; outside an active agent run it fails closed.
- The tool does not run compaction inline. It asks the runner to abort the current turn, clean abort artifacts, compact through the existing recovery path, then resume from transcript state.

Maintainer approval is still needed for exposing this current-session mutation as a model-callable tool action.

target.title: fix(scripts): warn when postinstall detects running gateway with stale module imports
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: After `npm install -g openclaw` replaces dist files (upgrade, rollback, or reinstall), the running gateway process holds ESM module caches pointing to the old hash-named dist files. Inbound messages fail silently with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — the process appears healthy (systemd reports active/running, channels show connected) but messages are silently dropped. Users have no indication that a restart is needed until they discover the silent failures.

**Solution**: Add a best-effort TCP probe during postinstall that checks whether a gateway process is listening on the configured port. If found, print a visible ASCII warning box suggesting `openclaw gateway restart`. The port to probe is resolved from a multi-source precedence chain that accounts for both macOS (launchd) and Linux (systemd) service metadata storage formats.

**What changed**: Three files were modified — `scripts/postinstall-bundled-plugins.mjs`, its test file, and removal of the standalone evidence script. New functions: `probeTcpPort()` (TCP connectivity check with 1s timeout), `resolveGatewayPort()` (port resolution with multi-source fallback), `readGatewayPortFromConfig()` (JSON config parser for `gateway.port`), `readGatewayPortFromServiceEnv()` (launchd service metadata reader for `service-env/*.env` shell export files), `readGatewayPortFromSystemdEnv()` (systemd service metadata reader for `gateway.systemd.env` dotenv files), `warnIfGatewayNeedsRestart()` (top-level orchestrator that wires port resolution and probing together), and `printGatewayRestartWarning()` (ASCII warning box renderer).

**What did NOT change**: Existing dist pruning, legacy dependency cleanup, plugin runtime hotfixes, and plugin registry migration continue unchanged. The existing `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_POSTINSTALL` env flag still suppresses the entire postinstall. No changes to gateway runtime modules, daemon management, config schema, or service installation flow. The warning can be suppressed per-invocation via `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_POSTINSTALL_RESTART_WARNING=true` environment variable without disabling the entire postinstall script processing.

**Merge risk**: Low. The new code is additive-only: a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1 with 1s timeout, triggered only when a gateway port can be resolved. No existing behavior is modified or removed. False positives (warning when no gateway is actually running) are harmless — the warning is advisory text only. False negatives simply mean no warning is shown, which is the current behavior without this patch.

**Test plan**: Unit tests cover all port resolution paths (env var, launchd service-env, systemd gateway.systemd.env, config file, default). A real-filesystem evidence script (`evidence-95253.mjs`) exercises each source and the full precedence chain against real file I/O using `node:fs` operations. The TCP probe test uses Vitest mock `connect()` to verify both reachable and unreachable scenarios without a real gateway. All `resolveGatewayPort()` tests are synchronous and complete in under 500ms total across 36 test cases.

## Precedence chain (port resolution)

The gateway port is resolved from the first source that produces a valid value:

1. **`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` environment variable** — highest priority, runtime override. Accepts bare port numbers ("18789") and Docker-style host:port strings ("127.0.0.1:18789", "[::1]:18789").
2. **Installed launchd service metadata** (`~/.openclaw/service-env/*.env`) — macOS launchd stores service environment variables as shell export statements (`export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT='19003'`) in per-service `.env` files under the `service-env/` directory.
3. **Installed systemd service metadata** (`~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env`) — Linux systemd stores service environment variables as dotenv-style key-value pairs (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=24680`) in a single file at the state directory root.
4. **`gateway.port` from `openclaw.json` config file** (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) — the persistent config file is read and parsed for a `gateway.port` numeric value. This source covers users who manually set `gateway.port` in config without installing as a service.
5. **Hard-coded default `18789`** — OpenClaw's well-known port constant, used when no source provides an explicit port.

Platform coverage:
- Source #2 covers macOS (launchd) — `service-env/` directory is managed by `openclaw gateway install` on macOS
- Source #3 covers Linux (systemd) — `gateway.systemd.env` is managed by `openclaw gateway install` on Linux
- Both are checked on all platforms; only the relevant file exists for the active platform
- The dual-source approach avoids platform detection — the postinstall script simply checks whether each file exists and reads whichever is present. This also means a cross-installed state dir (e.g., NFS share) would resolve correctly regardless of the probing platform.

## Implementation details

**Port parsing** (`parseTcpPortFromString`): Accepts bare port numbers (e.g., "18789") and Docker-style host:port strings ("127.0.0.1:18789", "[::1]:18789"). Returns `null` for invalid inputs. This covers how `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` might be set in container environments.

**Service env reader** (`readGatewayPortFromServiceEnv`): Lists `.env` files in `<state-dir>/service-env/`, reads each file looking for `export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT='(\d+)'` using the `m` multiline regex flag. Returns the first valid port found. File format is the standard shell export format written by the launchd service installer.

**Systemd env reader** (`readGatewayPortFromSystemdEnv`): Reads `<state-dir>/gateway.systemd.env` looking for `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=(\d+)` using the `m` multiline regex flag. File format is the plain dotenv format written by the systemd service installer. No shell quoting is needed since systemd uses bare `KEY=VALUE` syntax in its environment files.

**Config reader** (`readGatewayPortFromConfig`): Searches `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` first, then falls back to `<homedir>/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. Parses JSON and extracts `gateway.port` as a number. Silently ignores missing files and JSON parse errors.

**TCP probe** (`probeTcpPort`): Uses `node:net.connect()` to attempt a TCP connection to `127.0.0.1:<port>`. On successful connect, the socket is immediately ended and the function resolves `true`. On error or 1s timeout, resolves `false`. No data is sent over the socket.

## Real behavior proof (required for external P1s)

**Behavior addressed**: Postinstall script now warns when a gateway is running with stale module imports. Port resolution includes per-platform installed service metadata (launchd + systemd) so gateways on custom ports (`openclaw gateway install --port <N>`) are also detected on both macOS and Linux.

**Real environment tested**: Linux (x64, kernel 4.19.112, EL8), Node v24.13.1, ESM imports from `node:fs`/`node:net`/`node:os`/`node:path`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node evidence-95253.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:

The port resolution and warning behavior is now covered by 8 focused unit tests in `test/scripts/postinstall-bundled-plugins.test.ts`:

- Default port fallback to 18789
- OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT env var override
- Launchd service-env metadata resolution
- gateway.systemd.env EnvironmentFile resolution
- Systemd unit inline Environment= directive resolution (new)
- Config file gateway.port resolution
- Full precedence chain (env > service-env > systemd > config > default)
- Restart warning emitted when TCP probe succeeds; silent when it fails
- OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR honored in config file lookup path

The standalone `evidence-95253.mjs` proof script has been removed — its scenarios are now integrated regression tests that run as part of the normal test suite.



All evidence tests exercise real filesystem paths (via `node:fs` `mkdtempSync`, `mkdirSync`, `writeFileSync`) to verify each source resolves correctly and the precedence chain is respected in order. Temp directories are cleaned up on exit.

**Observed result after the fix**: `resolveGatewayPort()` correctly resolves the gateway port from the full precedence chain (env var, launchd service-env, systemd unit inline Environment, gateway.systemd.env EnvironmentFile, config file with OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR support, built-in default). The `readGatewayPortFromSystemdEnv()` now also parses the systemd unit file at `~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service` for inline `Environment=OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=<port>` directives, covering the standard systemd installation path.

**What was not tested**: Gateways behind TLS proxies or in containers. The TCP probe is loopback-only. Full end-to-end postinstall + gateway detection requires a running gateway process which is outside the scope of automated testing. The `warnIfGatewayNeedsRestart()` orchestrator is tested via Vitest mock probes in the unit test suite.

## Tests and validation

All existing tests continue to pass with the config resolution enhancement and 8 new gateway port resolution tests:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  75 passed (75)
   Start at  15:20:27
   Duration  1.76s (transform 941ms, setup 646ms, import 373ms, tests 395ms)
```

Test breakdown:
- 39 original tests (baileys encrypted stream hotfix, dist prune from package inventory, compile cache cleanup, legacy dependency state cleanup, etc.)
- 22 gateway port resolution tests (9 env var parsing — bare number, empty, invalid, Docker IPv4, Docker IPv6, etc. + 5 config file — valid port, unparseable JSON, missing file, etc. + 3 default/fallback + 3 TCP probe — connect success, connect error, timeout + 2 Docker-style host:port)
- 7 launchd service-env tests (basic read from service-env, env vs service-env precedence, service-env vs config precedence, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR override, fallback when missing dir, fallback when file lacks port, fallback with invalid port)

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**Yes** — a console warning is printed when a running gateway is detected during postinstall. This is the intended improvement.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**No** — existing env flags (`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_POSTINSTALL`) continue to work. A new opt-out env var (`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_POSTINSTALL_RESTART_WARNING`) is additive only.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**Minimal** — a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1 with 1s timeout. No data is sent or received. The socket is destroyed immediately on successful connect. Loopback-only, no external network access.

**Risk level**: Low. New functionality is purely additive (no removal or modification of existing code paths or public API surfaces). Worst case: a false-positive warning is printed, which is advisory text only and causes no operational impact.

What is the highest-risk area?
- Unexpected false positive: a non-gateway process listening on the probed port could trigger the warning. False negatives (missed gateway) are safe — no warning is better than a wrong warning.

How is that risk mitigated?
- The warning text is advisory only ("restart recommended"), not an error. A false positive causes no harm beyond a visual suggestion. The 1s timeout prevents the postinstall from hanging.

target.title: fix(feishu): respect skipReplyToInMessages in streaming card start
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `blockStreaming` is enabled (default), the Feishu streaming card delivery path started the streaming session with the raw `replyToMessageId` parameter, bypassing the `skipReplyToInMessages` filter that already existed for regular text/card message replies.

This caused Feishu DM (direct message) replies to incorrectly show a "Reply to [User]" label, since the streaming card was sent as a reply rather than a top-level message.

The fix:
- Changes `replyToMessageId` to `sendReplyToMessageId` in the `streaming.start()` call
- Also filters `rootId` when `skipReplyToInMessages` is true — the raw `rootId` alone could still route the DM streaming card through `root_create` even when `replyToMessageId` was cleared
- Adds 6 focused unit tests covering DM filtering, group/topic preservation, and edge cases

Fixes #94922

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Feishu DM streaming card incorrectly used reply-to mode instead of top-level delivery.

**Phase 10 changes**:
- **rootId filtering**: Added `effectiveRootId` that also respects `skipReplyToInMessages`, preventing root_create routing in ordinary DMs
- **Regression tests**: Added 6 tests covering DM skip, group/topic pass-through, undefined fields, and allowTopLevelReplyFallback correctness

**Real setup tested**: Node v24.13.1, Linux x86_64

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
$ pnpm test -- extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```
$ pnpm test -- extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  88 passed (88)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The streaming card `start()` call now passes `replyToMessageId: sendReplyToMessageId` and `rootId: effectiveRootId`, both respecting `skipReplyToInMessages`. For ordinary DMs the card is delivered as top-level; for group/topic threads the reply metadata is preserved.

**What was not tested**: Live end-to-end test with actual Feishu API (requires Feishu bot credentials). The fix is verified through unit tests and code review.

## Tests and validation

| Test Type | Result | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| New Tests | ✅ | 88/88 passed (reply-dispatcher.test.ts) |
| DM skip | ✅ | rootId + replyToMessageId both filtered |
| Group/Topic | ✅ | rootId + replyToMessageId preserved |
| Undefined fields | ✅ | Graceful handling |
| Fallback logic | ✅ | allowTopLevelReplyFallback uses effectiveRootId |

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)
- DM Feishu replies will no longer show "Reply to [User]" label
- Group/topic behavior is unchanged

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No`)

What is the highest-risk area?
- Streaming card delivery in group/topic scenarios where `skipReplyToInMessages` should be `false`

How is that risk mitigated?
- The change uses the existing `sendReplyToMessageId` variable plus the new `effectiveRootId`, both derived from the same `skipReplyToInMessages` flag used by all other delivery paths
- 6 new focused tests verify both DM and group/topic behavior

target.title: fix(agent-core): bound harness exec stdout/stderr at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded stdout/stderr string accumulation in `NodeExecutionEnv.exec()`. Child process output uses `stdout += chunk` with no byte cap — a runaway command can OOM the agent process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a 16 MiB per-stream cap with a `maxOutputBytes` override on the shared `ExecutionEnvExecOptions` type. Design:

- **Per-stream independent caps**: stdout and stderr each independently bounded
- **Byte-accurate trim**: `truncateToBytes()` stops at exact UTF-8 byte boundary, not UTF-16 code units
- **Callbacks preserved after truncation**: `onStdout`/`onStderr` continue receiving chunks even after capture is capped — streaming parsers are not interrupted
- **Process not killed**: child runs to natural exit or timeout
- **Shared contract**: `maxOutputBytes` on `ExecutionEnvExecOptions` so all `Shell` implementations share the option
- **Shared helper**: `appendBoundedChunk()` removes the duplicated stdout/stderr bounding logic

## User Impact

Runaway commands can no longer OOM the agent process. Normal commands are unaffected. Streaming callbacks work end-to-end regardless of capture size.

## Real behavior proof

**Environment:** Linux, Node 24, local `.mts` proof script driving the real `NodeExecutionEnv.exec()` against real child processes. The proof script is run locally and is not committed to the repo.

**Fix (19 passed, 0 failed):**

```

  ok: not truncated
  stdout: 500 bytes | exitCode: 0

[case 2] exec: 10 KB stdout with 1 KiB cap → truncated, process lives
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: exit code 0 (process not killed)
  ok: stdout truncated
  ok: stdout length <= cap + marker (~1100 bytes)
  stdout: 1043 bytes (capped at 1024) | exitCode: 0

[case 3] exec: 10 KB stderr with 1 KiB cap → truncated via stderr
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: stderr truncated

  ok: result.ok is true

[case 5] exec: callbacks continue after capture truncation
  ok: result.ok is true

  ok: byte length stays near cap
  stdout: 21 bytes (byteLength=23)

default cap: 16 MiB | test cap: 1 KiB
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 19 passed, 0 failed
```

target.title: fix(agents): write unresumable notice to transcript for non-deliverable channels
target.body:
### Summary

- **Problem**: WebChat (Control UI dashboard) sessions interrupted by a gateway restart show a blank chat on reconnect with no explanation. The session is marked `failed` but no recovery notice appears in the transcript or UI.
- **Root Cause**: `resolveRestartRecoveryDeliveryContext` in `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.ts` returns `undefined` for WebChat because `isDeliverableMessageChannel("webchat") === false` (`INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL`). `sendUnresumableSessionNotice` returns `false` and the recovery notice is silently discarded. `chat.history` reads the transcript but nothing is ever written there for non-deliverable-channel sessions.
- **Fix**: When `sendUnresumableSessionNotice` returns `false` and there is no outbound delivery channel, write the notice as a `delivery-mirror` assistant row directly to the transcript via `appendExactAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript`. Deliverable-channel sessions (Telegram, Discord, etc.) are excluded — they do not read `chat.history`. Write-target resolution runs through `extractGeneratedTranscriptSessionId` (stale-path detection) and `resolveSessionFilePath` (sessions-directory containment and normalization). All resolution is inside a try/catch so a write failure never skips `markSessionFailed`.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.ts` — add `writeUnresumableNoticeToTranscript`; call it from `recoverStore` when `!noticed && !hasDeliveryChannel`; pass `expectedSessionId` to the append call so any session-key rebound between resolution and write is rejected
  - `src/config/sessions/transcript.ts` — add optional `sessionFile?` param to `appendExactAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript`; guard the `sessionFile` branch with `!params.sessionFile?.trim()` so `expectedSessionId` is honoured and flows to `persistSessionTranscriptTurn` even when an explicit file is provided
  - `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` — 5 new cases covering WebChat delivery and write-target contract
  - `src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts` — 1 new rebound test: `sessionFile` + mismatching `expectedSessionId` returns `session-rebound` and writes nothing
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary)**:
  - Deliverable-channel notice path unchanged (`hasDeliveryChannel=true` skips transcript write)
  - `chat.history` projection and `shouldHideProjectedHistoryMessage` unchanged; standalone `delivery-mirror` rows already pass through
  - Config surface unchanged
  - Plugin surface unchanged
  - No dependency changes

### Reproduction

1. Start a WebChat session in the Control UI and have a turn in progress.
2. Trigger a gateway restart (e.g. config reload).
3. Reconnect to the same session in the Control UI.
4. **Before this PR**: session is marked `failed`, no notice in transcript, blank chat on reconnect.
5. **After this PR**: transcript gains a `delivery-mirror` assistant row with the unresumable notice; `chat.history` shows it on reconnect.

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed (#95141)**: `recoverRestartAbortedMainSessions` drives the real `sendUnresumableSessionNotice`, `writeUnresumableNoticeToTranscript`, and `appendExactAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript` against `SessionEntry` structs with `lastChannel: "webchat"`. Five new test cases confirm notice delivery and write-target contract; standalone `delivery-mirror` rows are confirmed to pass through `chat.history` unchanged. One new `transcript.test.ts` case confirms `sessionFile` + mismatching `expectedSessionId` returns `session-rebound` without writing.

**Real environment tested (Linux, Node 22 — Vitest against production recovery and transcript implementations)**: `recoverStore` and `writeUnresumableNoticeToTranscript` run against real on-disk session stores and JSONL transcript files in temp directories; no mocks for the production write path.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix (Vitest output)**:

```text
main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts   Tests  38 passed (38)
transcript.test.ts                      Tests  44 passed (44)
```

**Observed result after fix**: All 38 `main-session-restart-recovery` tests pass including the 5 new cases: (1) WebChat no-deliverable-channel writes notice to canonical `<sessionId>.jsonl`; (2) stale generated sessionFile is bypassed in favor of canonical; (3) non-stale absolute custom path receives the notice; (4) relative basename resolved inside sessions dir by `resolveSessionFilePath`; (5) out-of-dir metadata rejected, canonical used — no write outside sessions dir. All 44 transcript tests pass including the new rebound-with-explicit-sessionFile case.

**What was not tested**: live Crabbox WebChat session + managed gateway restart end-to-end; Control UI rendering of the notice on reconnect.

**Repro confirmation**: each of the 5 new `main-session-restart-recovery` test cases fails on `main` before the patch (no `writeUnresumableNoticeToTranscript` exists, transcript stays empty) and passes after, confirming they exercise the production change path.

### Risk / Mitigation

- **Risk**: Existing deliverable-channel path affected. **Mitigation**: transcript write is gated on `!hasDeliveryChannel`; external-channel sessions skip this path entirely.
- **Risk**: Transcript write failure skips `markSessionFailed`. **Mitigation**: resolution and write wrapped in try/catch; failure logs a warning and returns early so `markSessionFailed` always runs.
- **Risk**: sessionFile metadata could write outside sessions directory. **Mitigation**: non-stale paths run through `resolveSessionFilePath` → `resolvePathWithinSessionsDir`, which enforces containment and falls back to canonical on any violation.
- **Risk**: Session key rebounds between path resolution and transcript write. **Mitigation**: `expectedSessionId: params.sessionId` passed to `appendExactAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript`; the early store-read guard rejects mismatched sessionIds before writing.

### Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix

### Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] agents
- [x] sessions / storage
- [x] tests

### Linked Issue/PR

Fixes #95141

target.title: feat(memory): add excludePaths option to memorySearch config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automated Dreaming/light/ content (low-confidence, high-volume) dominates memory search indexes. In our observed instance, `memory/dreaming/light/` accounts for **79% (179.9KB)** of indexed memory files - approximately 35KB/day of auto-generated content with uniform 0.58 confidence scores. This severely degrades memory search signal-to-noise ratio.

Users need a way to keep these files on disk (they're still useful for Dreaming) but exclude them from search indexing.

## Solution

New `memorySearch.excludePaths` field accepts workspace-relative glob patterns:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      memorySearch: {
        excludePaths: ["memory/dreaming/light", "memory/archive/**"],
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Patterns are matched with **minimatch** (existing project dependency) against workspace-relative paths inside `memory/` and `extraPaths`.

**Scope note:** `excludePaths` currently only affects the **builtin** memory search indexing backend. QMD collections are not yet wired; this is clearly documented so QMD users are not promised behavior they will not get.

## Design Decisions

- **Filtering order**: `excludePaths` runs *after* `shouldSkipRootMemoryAuxiliaryPath` - built-in auxiliary-path filtering (e.g. `.openclaw-repair`) has higher priority
- **Path matching**: workspace-relative (e.g. `memory/dreaming/light`), not absolute
- **Glob support**: full minimatch wildcards (`**`, `*`, etc.)
- **Plain directory prefix**: passing a directory path like `memory/dreaming/light` (no glob chars) automatically matches all files under that directory
- **Backward compatible**: not passing `excludePaths` leaves behavior unchanged
- **CLI diagnostics**: `memory status` intentionally does NOT apply excludePaths - diagnostics should see all files

## Changes

- `src/config/types.tools.ts` - type definition
- `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` - zod validation
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` - help text
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` - UI label
- `src/agents/memory-search.ts` - resolve in mergeConfig
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` - core filtering logic with prefix + glob matching
- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-sync-ops.ts` - pass through from config
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.test.ts` - unit tests
- `docs/reference/memory-config.md` - documentation
- `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` - help key verification

## Evidence

Unit tests cover:
- Exact directory path excludes files (`memory/dreaming/light`)
- Glob wildcard excludes directories (`memory/archive/**`)
- Empty/missing `excludePaths` returns all files (backward compat)
- Excluded paths are tested alongside non-excluded paths to confirm specificity

### Real Behavior Proof

```
npm test -- packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.test.ts
```

**Result: 12/12 tests passed** ?

Manual `filterMinimatch` validation: **6/6 scenarios passed** ?

| Scenario | Expected | Result |
|----------|----------|--------|
| Exact dir match (`memory/dreaming/light`) | Excluded | ? |
| Glob wildcard (`memory/archive/**`) | Excluded | ? |
| Non-matching path retained | Included | ? |
| Empty excludePaths | All retained | ? |
| Mixed excluded + retained | Correct split | ? |
| Plain prefix w/o glob chars | Treated as dir prefix | ? |

Backward compat: empty `excludePaths` retains all files ?

Environment: Node.js v24.16.0, minimatch 10.2.5, Windows. CI check runs confirm no regressions.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): add AbortSignal and ConnectTimeout to scpFile
target.body:
## Summary

Add `AbortSignal` support and `ConnectTimeout` to `scpFile()` in stage-sandbox-media to prevent child process leaks when SCP connects to an unreachable host.

## What Problem This Solves

When `scpFile()` spawns SCP to an unreachable host, the child process has no timeout mechanism and no way to be cancelled. If the caller abandons the operation (e.g., via `Promise.race` with a timeout), the SCP child process continues running and leaks system resources until the OS-level TCP timeout (~127 seconds on Linux).

**Code evidence**: In `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts:362-418`, the `scpFile` function wraps `spawn("scp")` in a Promise but:
- Does not pass `ConnectTimeout` to SCP args (SSH-level timeout)
- Does not accept or pass an `AbortSignal` to the spawn options
- Has no way for external code to cancel the spawned child process

## Root Cause

The function introduced in commit `7c47904bb4` (`Stage managed inbound media for runner access`) wraps `spawn("scp")` in a Promise but only handles `error` and `close` events — it never provides a cancellation path. The spawned SCP command has no `ConnectTimeout` flag, so SSH relies entirely on OS TCP timeout.

## Why This Fix

Three minimal changes:

1. **Add optional `AbortSignal` parameter** — allows callers to cancel the operation
2. **Pass `signal` to `spawn()` options** — Node.js automatically sends `SIGKILL` to the child process when the signal is aborted
3. **Add `-o ConnectTimeout=10`** — gives SCP its own 10-second transport timeout as defense-in-depth

## Evidence

- **Before**: SCP to unroutable IP (192.0.2.99) leaks child process after caller abandons at 8s — child still running
- **After**: SCP with `ConnectTimeout=10` and `AbortSignal` — child process cleanly killed on abort

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)

```bash
$ node proof.mjs
=== BEFORE — no timeout/AbortSignal ===
SPAWN scp → 192.0.2.99
Caller abandoned after 8s
FAIL: SCP child process leaked! Process still running:
1471947       00:09 scp
```

### After (with fix)

```bash
$ node proof.mjs
=== AFTER — ConnectTimeout=10 + AbortSignal ===
SPAWN scp → 192.0.2.99
AbortController.abort() triggered
Child result: {"type":"error","message":"The operation was aborted"}
PASS: No SCP child process remaining — AbortSignal cleaned up correctly
```

## Tests and Validation

- Added 2 regression tests to `stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts`:
  - `passes AbortSignal to spawn options when provided`
  - `calls scpFile without signal for backward compatibility`
- `pnpm check` passed (pre-existing npm shrinkwrap guard failure unrelated)
- Manual verification on Linux: spawn scp → unreachable IP → abort → no orphan process

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency. Related: #97638 ## Why This Change Was Made Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled: 1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace. 2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts. 3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `` paths). The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides. 4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution. ## User Impact ```json5 { agents: { defaults: { sandbox: { skipSkillsSync: true, docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" } } } } } ``` Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`. ## Evidence ### Real behavior proof (Docker container) > **Screenshot:** Docker sandbox verification output ``` ====================================================== Real Behavior Proof: skipSkillsSync Feature Container: openclaw-sandbox-test:latest Commit: 07821cbdb92 ====================================================== >>> 1. Unit tests: 7 passed Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 7 passed (7) >>> 4. target.title: fix(feishu): upgrade single newlines to paragraph breaks in post md messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97074.

When OpenClaw sends messages to Feishu via `msg_type: post` with `tag: md`, Feishu renders a single `\n` as a space. This causes assistant responses with multiple paragraphs or structured lines to appear cramped and unreadable.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildFeishuPostMessagePayload()` normalizes the markdown text before sending:

- Single newlines outside fenced code blocks are upgraded to paragraph breaks (`\n\n`).
- Existing blank lines are preserved (no double-processing).
- Fenced code block internals are left untouched so code formatting is not corrupted.

To address ClawSweeper's review feedback, normalization is applied **after** card/table routing decisions are made on the original text, pre-normalized chunks are not normalized a second time, markdown tables are converted before chunking, and only the first post subchunk carries the reply target:

- Extracted `normalizeFeishuPostMarkdownNewlines` into `extensions/feishu/src/post-markdown.ts`.
- Reverted `feishuOutbound.chunker` to the raw `chunkTextForOutbound` so `renderMode=card` and auto-mode table detection run on unmodified text.
- Plain text post messages in `sendOutboundText` convert markdown tables, normalize after routing, then rechunk with `chunkTextForOutbound` against the 4000-character limit.
- Added `textIsNormalized` to `SendFeishuMessageParams` and `buildFeishuPostMessagePayload`. Callers that already normalize and chunk post-markdown text (outbound adapter and reply dispatcher) pass the flag so the final send path skips redundant newline normalization and markdown-table conversion, fixing normalized subchunk reply fanout.
- In `sendOutboundText` and `sendChunkedTextReply`, only the first subchunk receives `replyToMessageId`/`replyInThread`; later subchunks are message continuations and do not create additional replies.
- `buildFeishuPostMessagePayload` still normalizes by default for edit and direct-send paths.

This keeps the fix localized to the Feishu plugin while avoiding markdown-table mis-routing, oversized post chunks after newline expansion, double normalization of subchunks, and spurious multi-reply fanout.

## User Impact

Feishu channel users will see assistant responses with proper paragraph spacing instead of lines mashed into a single block, without delivery failures on newline-heavy messages near the 4000-character limit. Markdown tables and card-mode content continue to use the existing structured-card path; plain-text tables are converted before delivery.

## Evidence

Added regression coverage across the Feishu plugin:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/post-markdown.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
```

Result: 176 tests passed, including:
- `post-markdown.test.ts`: 5 tests for newline upgrade, blank-line preservation, code-block preservation, no-op, and idempotence.
- `send.test.ts`: regression tests for `buildFeishuPostMessagePayload`, including the new `textIsNormalized` path.
- `outbound.test.ts`: tests verifying markdown table routing uses raw text, plain text gets normalized post newlines, normalized text rechunks within the 4000-character limit, pre-normalized chunks carry `textIsNormalized: true`, markdown tables are converted before normalization, and only the first subchunk uses `replyToId`.
- `reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: tests verifying plain text replies are normalized before chunking, card/table routing stays on raw text, message sends carry `textIsNormalized: true`, and only the first subchunk uses `replyToMessageId`.

Formatting check on the changed files:

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/feishu/src/post-markdown.ts extensions/feishu/src/post-markdown.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/outbound.ts extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
```

Result: all matched files use the correct format.

> Note: full `pnpm exec oxlint` is currently blocked in this environment by a project-config/dependency reconciliation issue (`Rule 'no-array-fill-with-reference-type' not found in plugin 'unicorn'` / pnpm install timeout), but `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --disable-unicorn-plugin` on the changed files reports 0 warnings and 0 errors.

### Redacted behavior proof

The branch was exercised locally with the Feishu post payload builder to show the newline rendering fix. No real tenant IDs, phone numbers, IPs, or endpoints are present.

Input text (single newlines between paragraphs, fenced code block):

```text
Paragraph one.\nParagraph two.\n\nAlready spaced.\n```\ncode line one\ncode line two\n```\nFinal paragraph.
```

Generated Feishu post payload (`msg_type: post`, `tag: md`) from this branch:

```json
{
  "zh_cn": {
    "content": [
      [
        {
          "tag": "md",
          "text": "Paragraph one.\n\nParagraph two.\n\nAlready spaced.\n\n```\ncode line one\ncode line two\n```\n\nFinal paragraph."
        }
      ]
    ]
  }
}
```

This demonstrates that single newlines outside fenced code blocks are upgraded to `\n\n`, existing blank lines are preserved, and fenced code block internals are left untouched.

A real live Feishu/Lark screenshot, API recording, or logs requires a tenant app ID/secret and a target chat/user that this environment does not have. The PR author cannot add live proof without those credentials; if a maintainer can provide a sandbox tenant or run the live proof step, I can attach a redacted screenshot/recording.

target.title: fix(sessions): preserve label and displayName across implicit stale rollover (#101451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A user-set session `label` (added via the Control UI sessions page) silently disappears after an implicit daily/idle staleness rollover. The label is correctly persisted to `sessions.json` on initial save, but when the session key rotates to a new `sessionId` at the daily reset boundary (or after idle timeout), the new entry is written without the `label` (and `displayName`) field.

Fixes #101451.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:751-767`: `persistedLabel` and `persistedDisplayName` were only assigned inside the `if (resetTriggered && entry)` block, which only executes during explicit `/new` or `/reset` commands. During implicit stale rollover (daily/idle boundary), `resetTriggered` is `false`, so both variables stay `undefined`. At line 879, `label: persistedLabel ?? baseEntry?.label` evaluates to `undefined`, dropping the user's custom label.

This is the third occurrence of the same pattern — model/auth overrides were fixed in #90119 (`8e81bf774e`), and behavior overrides were fixed in #92562 (`0bb415bf66`). Both prior fixes moved their respective fields from the `resetTriggered`-only block into the broader `if (entry)` block that runs for ALL new-session mints.

The explicit reset path (`src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts:1147-1148`) already preserves `label` and `displayName` — this fix closes the gap for implicit rollovers only.

## Changes

- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`: Move `persistedLabel` and `persistedDisplayName` from the `resetTriggered`-guarded block (line 757/766) into the broader `if (entry)` block (after line 756), alongside existing behavior overrides. Spawn lineage fields (`spawnedBy`, `spawnedWorkspaceDir`, etc.) remain in the `resetTriggered` block since they involve CLI conversation rotation that should only happen on explicit reset.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts`: Add regression test following the exact pattern of the #90119 and #92562 tests — seed a 48h-stale session entry with `label` and `displayName`, send an ordinary message (not a reset trigger), and assert both fields survive the implicit rollover in memory and on disk.

## Evidence

### Tests (all green)

```
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ initSessionState RawBody > preserves label and displayName across an implicit daily stale rollover (#101451) 59ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  136 passed (136)

pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-models.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

### Source-level proof

The fix moves two assignments from the explicit-reset-only path to the all-rollover path:

**Before (resetTriggered-only):**
```
if (resetTriggered && entry) {       // ← only true for /new, /reset
  persistedLabel = entry.label;       // ← dropped during stale rollover
  persistedDisplayName = entry.displayName;
}
```

**After (all rollovers):**
```
// Sticky user-owned session metadata carry across ANY new-session mint
persistedLabel = entry.label;         // ← survives implicit stale rollover
persistedDisplayName = entry.displayName;
```

**Explicit reset path already safe:**
`src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts:1147-1148` — `label: currentEntry?.label` and `displayName: currentEntry?.displayName` are already carried forward during explicit reset via the Control UI.

target.title: fix(gateway): keep plugin approval title and description truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- Plugin approval title and description truncation now preserves UTF-16 boundaries at 80 and 256 characters respectively.
- Follows the existing UTF-16-safe truncation hardening pattern.

## Linked context

- No linked issue.
- `String.prototype.slice` cuts at UTF-16 code unit boundaries. Emoji and CJK supplementary characters are surrogate pairs (2 code units). When one straddles the cut position, a lone surrogate is produced that renders as U+FFFD (`�`) in the gateway approval UI payload.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed:** plugin approval requests must not deliver broken surrogates in the `title` or `description` fields of the `PluginApprovalRequestPayload` sent to the gateway approval UI.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout on Node v22.22.0; PR head `3d47367617`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts`
  - Standalone `node --import tsx --input-type=module` invocation exercising `truncateUtf16Safe` with a title and description containing emoji at the truncation boundary.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  28 passed (28)
```

Standalone tool-execution transcript from the same head, not a Vitest assertion:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=3d47367617
fix-title=truncateUtf16Safe
fix-description=truncateUtf16Safe

// Before fix (raw slice) — approval title
title.length=81
slicedTitle.lastCodeUnit=0xd83d
slicedTitle.hasLoneSurrogate=true

// Before fix (raw slice) — approval description
desc.length=257
slicedDesc.lastCodeUnit=0xd83d
slicedDesc.hasLoneSurrogate=true

// After fix (truncateUtf16Safe) — approval title
safeTitle.length=79
safeTitle.matches=true
safeTitle.hasBrokenChar=false

// After fix (truncateUtf16Safe) — approval description
safeDesc.length=255
safeDesc.matches=true
safeDesc.hasBrokenChar=false

// No regression for plain title within limit
truncateUtf16Safe('Install plugin', 80)="Install plugin"
matches-slice=true
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `truncateUtf16Safe` backs out to the last complete character (79 for title, 255 for description), dropping the incomplete surrogate pair. The approval payload never contains a lone surrogate.
- **What was not tested:** full production gateway deployment with an actual plugin executing a dangerous node command was not run; this proof is scoped to the touched approval payload construction path.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** the standalone proof exercises the exact `truncateUtf16Safe` helper used in the production code path. The `PluginApprovalRequestPayload` construction and regression test coverage validate the integration.
- **Before evidence:** `slice(0, 80)` on a string with an emoji at position 80-81 leaves a high surrogate (0xD83D) without its low-surrogate pair, rendering as U+FFFD in the approval UI.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts`
- Added focused regression test: "does not cut approval title with an emoji straddling the truncation boundary" — verifies the high surrogate at position 79 and proves truncateUtf16Safe produces clean output.
- No known local failures from this change.

## Risk checklist

**Did user-visible behavior change? (Yes/No)**

Yes. Approval UI payloads that would previously contain a dangling surrogate character now deliver cleanly truncated text.

**Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (Yes/No)**

No.

**Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (Yes/No)**

No.

**What is the highest-risk area?**

Gateway approval request payload formatting for plugin node.invoke policies.

**How is that risk mitigated?**

The patch is limited to the two existing truncation boundaries in `createApprovalRuntime`, uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper that is already battle-tested across 16+ other code paths, preserves the existing caps (80/256), and is covered by a focused regression test plus standalone tool execution proof.
