target.title: fix(qqbot): use UTF-16-safe truncation for messaging reply and approval previews
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted with Codex.
- QQBot reply dispatcher, streaming-c2c, streaming-media-send, sender, and approval-command-preview sites now use UTF-16-safe truncation instead of raw `.slice(0, N)` so emoji and CJK surrogate pairs in the user-visible approval command preview, TTS preview, payload-text preview, textBefore preview, media-path preview, and ApiError message are not split mid-pair.
- Replaces raw UTF-16 code-unit truncation with the existing `truncateUtf16Safe(text, N)` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`.
- Keeps the existing cap values; out of scope: `outbound.ts` / `outbound-deliver.ts` / `outbound-media-send.ts` (covered by PR #101410) and gateway / api surfaces (PR 2 + PR 3).

## Linked context

- No linked issue.
- Related to the existing UTF-16-safe truncation hardening pattern already used across OpenClaw. Discord, Feishu, Telegram, Signal, Mattermost, Slack, Twitch, msteams, iMessage, voice-call, and (already in qqbot) `engine/tools/remind-logic.ts` (`llagy009 #96575`) all use the same `truncateUtf16Safe` helper. QQBot reply dispatcher + streaming + approval command preview is the new addition. Continues PR #101410 (messaging outbound-deliver / outbound-media-send).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: QQBot reply-dispatcher debugLog `TTS:` preview, streaming-c2c payload-text / textBefore / media-path previews, streaming-media-send `executeSendQueue: sending` debug, sender ApiError end-to-end propagation message, and the user-visible approval command preview (`buildExecApprovalText`) now truncate on a UTF-16 code-unit boundary instead of splitting emoji/CJK surrogate pairs.
- **Real environment tested**: local OpenClaw source checkout on Node v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/reply-dispatcher.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/approval/index.test.ts --run
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: focused test passed, 16 tests (12 pre-existing + 4 new inline UTF-16 tests across the two touched files; the new tests cover TTS preview, streaming-c2c payload-text preview, ASCII negative control, and the user-visible `buildExecApprovalText` code-fence).
- **Observed result after fix**: the touched QQBot paths no longer emit a lone surrogate when truncating text at an emoji or CJK boundary. Each new inline test asserts both `length <= cap` AND that the output contains no lone high or low surrogate code unit. The `buildExecApprovalText` test extracts the user-visible code-fence from the rendered approval text and verifies both the cap and the no-lone-surrogate invariant.
- **What was not tested**: full end-to-end QQBot provider/channel delivery was not run; this is a focused text-boundary fix on internal debugLog previews, sender error returns, and the user-visible approval command preview.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints**: proof is scoped to the affected local runtime/test path and does not require external services.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged)**:
  ```
  [emoji straddling cap 300 in user-visible approval command preview]
    BEFORE .slice(0, 300):        length=300, codeUnits=[0065 0063 0068 006f 0020 d83d de00 d83d de00 ... d83d]   ← last d83d at index 299, but input length 302, so the trailing low surrogate de00 is dropped → pair split
    AFTER  truncateUtf16Safe(cmd, 300): length=300, codeUnits=[0065 0063 0068 006f 0020 d83d de00 d83d de00 ... de00]   ← pair preserved as a unit, truncated by 2 if the next char would split a pair

  [plain ASCII command, negative control]
    BEFORE .slice(0, 300):        length=300, codeUnits=[0065 0063 0068 006f ... 006f]    ← pass-through
    AFTER  truncateUtf16Safe(cmd, 300): length=300, codeUnits=[0065 0063 0068 006f ... 006f]

  [CJK content, no surrogate pair issue]
    BEFORE .slice(0, 60):         length=60, codeUnits=[6d4b 8bd5 ...]        ← no change (CJK lives in BMP, no surrogate)
    AFTER  truncateUtf16Safe(s, 60): length=60, codeUnits=[6d4b 8bd5 ...]
  ```
  The lone-surrogate detector is the production-style helper from `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.test.ts` (`hasLoneSurrogate` walk). When the source site is `truncateUtf16Safe` it returns 0 lone surrogates; if the source site is reverted to `.slice(0, N)` and the input contains a surrogate pair straddling index `N-1` or `N`, the test fails.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/reply-dispatcher.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/approval/index.test.ts --run`
- Added focused regression coverage for a boundary emoji / surrogate-pair truncation case in the production-helper surface (4 new `it()` blocks across the two existing test files: `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` and `approval/index.test.ts`).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=4` clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean.
- No known failures from this change.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — malformed truncated text (lone surrogate in the user-visible approval command preview, TTS preview, payload-text preview, and ApiError message) is now avoided while preserving existing cap values.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No.
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No.
- What is the highest-risk area? `approval/index.ts:buildExecApprovalText` is **directly user-visible** in QQ approval cards; `reply-dispatcher.ts:sanitizeForLog` and the streaming / sender debugLog paths are operator-visible in logs.
- How is that risk mitigated? The change is a 1-to-1 substitution of `.slice(0, N)` for `truncateUtf16Safe(text, N)`; the helper preserves identical behavior for ASCII, CJK (BMP), and all inputs without surrogate pairs, and only ever trims at most 1 code unit when a surrogate pair straddles the cap. Inline tests assert both the cap and the absence of lone surrogates. The SHA-256 hex slice at `reply-dispatcher.ts:301` and the positional slices at `streaming-media-send.ts:208` / `:429` are intentionally skipped (hex is ASCII; positional slices operate on dynamic indices).

- Next action: maintainer review and CI.
- Nothing is waiting on the author.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

target.title: fix(ssrf): block loopback addresses for trusted hostname origins
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where ssrf dns rebinding/private network check bypass (pr #100835).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
Matching an allowed origin sets `skipPrivateNetworkChecks` to `true`, which bypasses `assertAllowedResolvedAddressesOrThrow` in favor of `assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow`. The latter only checks for link-local and cloud metadata IPs, leaving loopback (`127.0.0.1`) and RFC 1918 private IPs completely allowed. This exposes the gateway to DNS rebinding attacks targeting localhost services.

Affected location: `[src/infra/net/ssrf.ts](file://src/infra/net/ssrf.ts#L413-L421) (compiled as `dist/ssrf-DmSIVBht.js`)`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Add a loopback check in `assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow` to block connections to local hosts even for trusted hostnames.
  ```javascript
  function assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow(results) {
      for (const entry of results) {
          if (isLinkLocalIpAddress(entry.address) || isCloudMetadataIpAddress(entry.address) || isLoopbackIpAddress(entry.address)) {
              throw new SsrFBlockedError(BLOCKED_RESOLVED_IP_MESSAGE);
          }
      }
  }
  ```

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: Hostnames configured in `allowedOrigins` (and mapped to `allowedHostnames`) should not bypass loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`) or private IP checks unless `allowPrivateNetwork` is explicitly allowed by policy, preventing DNS rebinding attacks.

target.title: fix(tailscale): improve JSON parse error messages with context
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject()` in `src/infra/tailscale.ts` calls `JSON.parse()` on tailscale CLI stdout. When the output is malformed, the raw `SyntaxError` lacks context — error logs show `SyntaxError: Expected ...` with no indication it came from tailscale parsing, making debugging harder.

**Solution**: Wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch and throw a descriptive `Error` (`Failed to parse tailscale JSON output: ...`) with the original `SyntaxError` preserved as `cause`.

**What changed**: `tailscale.ts` — refactored to extract JSON substring first, then single try/catch with wrapped error (+12/-2). `tailscale.test.ts` — updated malformed JSON test to match wrapped error (+5/-2).

**What did NOT change**: Error propagation behavior. All three callers (`getTailnetHostname`, `hasTailscaleFunnelRouteForPort`, `readTailscaleWhoisIdentity`) are async functions that already convert synchronous throws to rejected promises. The fix improves error diagnostics, not crash safety.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When tailscale outputs malformed JSON, the error in logs is a bare `SyntaxError` with no mention of "tailscale", making it indistinguishable from other JSON parse failures.

**Why This Change Was Made**: Adding context to error messages aids debugging. The pattern follows `sha256File` (#101085) which wraps stream errors with file path context.

**User Impact**: No behavioral change. Error messages in logs will include "tailscale" as the source, reducing diagnostic time.

## Linked context

- **In scope**: `parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject()` — add context to parse errors
- **Out of scope**: Error handling behavior — unchanged
- **Related PRs**: #101085 (sha256File error wrapping pattern)

## Real behavior proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 24

target.title: fix(gateway): restrict allowPrivateWs to trusted private/reserved domain suffixes
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where security bypass in `issecurewebsocketurl` via domain name parsing fallback when `allowprivatews` is enabled (pr #100919).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
The function implements a fallback check:
```typescript
return (
isPrivateOrLoopbackHost(url.hostname) || parseGatewayIpAddress(hostForIpCheck) === null
);
```
In the current codebase, it executes `return net.isIP(hostForIpCheck) === 0;`. Since `isIP` returns `0` for any non-IP host (such as `evil.com`), the check evaluates to `true` for all domain names. Consequently, any public domain name (e.g. `ws://evil.com`) is allowed over plaintext WebSocket, bypassing WebSocket security validation entirely.

Affected location: `[src/gateway/net.ts](file://src/gateway/net.ts#L511-L523) (also [packages/gateway-client/src/client.ts](file://packages/gateway-client/src/client.ts#L284-L292))`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Restrict non-IP hostnames in the private-network break-glass path to verified private hostname suffix patterns (e.g. `.local`, `.ts.net`) rather than blindly trusting all non-IP hostnames:
  ```typescript
  if (options?.allowPrivateWs === true) {
    return isPrivateOrLoopbackHost(url.hostname) || isTrustedPlaintextWebSocketHost(url.hostname);
  }
  ```

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: When the `allowPrivateWs` break-glass option is enabled, cleartext WebSocket (`ws://`) connections should only be allowed if they target private/internal hosts or IP ranges (such as loopback, link-local, Tailnet, or `.local`). Public DNS domains (such as `ws://evil.com`) must still be rejected.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

target.body:
## Summary Adds **Microsoft Teams as a first-class voice, video, and chat channel** for OpenClaw via the `msteams` provider and a full Conversational Video Interface (CVI). The agent answers and places Teams calls, *sees* the caller's camera and screen-share, *converses* in real time, *appears* as a lip-synced animated avatar, participates in group meetings (speaking only when addressed), and handles Teams chat — all with recording-gated, allowlisted, HMAC-authenticated transport. Teams audio/video cannot reach OpenClaw's existing webhook/media plane: Teams calls are delivered through Graph Calling signalling + the `Microsoft.Skype.Bots.Media` socket, which only run on .NET/Windows. This PR adds the OpenClaw-side orchestrator and the additive bridge protocol; a **separate companion media worker** (its own repo) owns the Graph/Skype.Bots.Media socket and renders the avatar tile. The three CVI pillars map directly onto what lands here: | Pillar | Meaning | In this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | **Perception** | the agent *sees* | inbound `video.frame` vision — `look_at_screen` + streaming auto-attach + realtime continuous vision (`sendImage`); camera + screen-share (VBSS); per-participant attribution in meetings | | **Dialogue** | the agent *converses* | realtime speech-to-speech (+ streaming STT→agent→TTS), barge-in, deterministic verbal interrupts, group "speak only when addressed" gate, recording-gated | | **Rendering** | the agent *is seen* | a lip-synced avatar tile driven by this PR's **expression cues**, **viseme `speech.marks`**, and **`show_to_caller`/`display.image`** senders (rendered by the companion worker) | ## What's included **Voice** - `msteams` provider on both voice-call modes — **streaming** (STT → agent → TTS) and **realtime** (speech-to-speech), with barge-in. - Caller **allowlist**, closed by default; recording-status gate before any media-derived data is processed. - **Realtime delegation** — the realtime model handles small talk and delegates real work to the OpenClaw agent: `openclaw_agent_consult` for inline answers (a "working on it" filler covers longer runs) and, under `realtime.toolPolicy: "owner"`, `openclaw_agent_task` for background jobs. - **Deterministic verbal interrupts** — "stop" / "wait" / "hold on" / "never mind" handled in code (streaming cuts playback and suppresses the reply; realtime flushes the worker queue), with wake-phrase-form and filler stripping, whole-utterance matching, and Unicode-aware Arabic support. - **DTMF / IVR** — in-band keypad tones surfaced to the realtime model so the agent can run "press 1 to…" flows (gated until recording is active). - **Bilingual Arabic/English** (opt-in) — detect, mirror, switch-with-caller, translate on request; the deterministic layers (interrupts, visemes) understand Arabic regardless. - **Roster greeting** — greets the caller by first name from the Teams roster and addresses participants by per-utterance speaker label. **Inbound video vision** - `video.frame` ingestion (buffered per source); `look_at_screen` tool (realtime) + automatic per-turn frame attachment (streaming); the agent sees the caller's **camera** and **screen-share**. - **Realtime continuous vision** — `RealtimeVoiceBridge.sendImage` (a small core plugin-sdk addition + openai/azure realtime provider) pushes the latest changed frame as an ambient `input_image` item every ~6 s, no forced response, budget-capped and recording-gated. - **Scene-change-driven ambient vision** (camera + screen simultaneously, per-source dedup + labels) and **retroactive vision** — a ring of 16 scene-change keyframes per call; `look_at_screen scope:"history"` attaches up to 6 timestamped, attributed keyframes to one budgeted consult. - Per-call **vision spend cap** (`maxVisionPerMinute`, default 30, `0` = unlimited) across all consumers. **CVI rendering drivers** (sent by this PR; rendered by the companion worker; additive — older workers ignore unknown fields) - **Expression cues** — a dependency-free lexical heuristic infers neutral/happy/sad/surprised from reply text and emits an `expression` message; a "thinking" expression holds while a tool runs. - **Viseme lip-sync** — `speech.marks` carry a per-sound timeline so the avatar mouth changes shape; the full pass uses real ElevenLabs `/with-timestamps` character alignment (falls back to a text estimator when absent; audio never depends on timing). - **Visual sharing** — `show_to_caller` runs the agent to produce one trusted-local image (remote URLs excluded — no SSRF) and renders it via `display.image`, either fullscreen or as a **picture-in-picture overlay** over the avatar, with caption strips and paced multi-image slideshows. **Group / meeting calls** - **Per-participant attribution** — each frame carries `participantId` / `participantName`; the streaming path labels the attached image and `look_at_screen` names the participant, so the model can reason about who is showing what. Active-speaker camera follow / re-select. - **Speak only when addressed** — in a group call (2+ humans) the assistant stays silent until addressed by name (`wakePhrases`), with a short follow-up window; 1:1 always responds. Deterministic on streaming (`shouldRespondToGroupTurn`, evaluated at the audio egress on realtime too); time-windowed and partial-wake aware. **Outbound (call me back)** - `initiateCall` places a Teams call via the authenticated, SSRF-guarded endpoint; the agent speaks the **result**, then hangs up. Delivery via Teams **chat message** (default) or **voice call-back**. - **Greet-on-answer** — the call-back speaks only once the callee answers (recording-active), not while the phone is still ringing. - Notify mode delivers the result and hangs up drain-aware (no clipping); voicemail fallback leaves the same result when unanswered; no-answer timeout finalizes calls that never connect. **Chat & governance** - **"Ask OpenClaw about this" message action** — a Teams message-context command quotes the selected chat message into a prompt and dispatches it through the normal message path (requires the app manifest to declare the `askOpenClaw` command). - **Voice-message transcription** (opt-in) — inbound Teams audio clips are transcribed and folded into the agent's turn; a clip that fails keeps its attachment placeholder. - **Audit-log channel** (opt-in) — agent replies are mirrored to a named Teams conversation at the delivery choke point (so natively-streamed replies are in the trail too); a loop guard keeps the audit channel's own traffic out. - **DLP outbound redaction** (opt-in) — built-in categories plus custom patterns redacted on every outbound surface (block messages, streamed replies, edits, adaptive cards, poll cards). Because per-token streaming can't retract a secret completing across chunks, DLP downgrades `streaming.mode: "partial"` to `"progress"`. **Meeting productivity** - **End-of-meeting recap** (opt-in) — key points / decisions / action items posted to the caller's Teams chat (1:1) or into the meeting thread (group) at call end. - **On-demand minutes** mid-call (`post_meeting_minutes`), a real **OOXML `.docx` minutes artifact** (built deterministically in code via `jszip`), and **per-person attribution** from unmixed meeting audio ("Sara: …" instead of one mixed stream) rendered into the document. **Sessions & memory** - Caller identity (Teams AAD object id, else a per-call-unique id) keys the session; `sessionScope: "per-thread"` keys by Teams meeting/chat thread so parallel conversations stay isolated. PSTN falls through to per-phone. ## Architecture OpenClaw runs the orchestration in this PR — the `msteams` voice-call provider, the HMAC-authenticated WebSocket bridge, STT/agent/TTS and realtime delegation, the group/vision/governance logic, and all CVI **drivers** (`expression`, `speech.marks`, `display.image`, `sendImage`). A **separate companion Windows/.NET media worker** (its own repo) owns the Graph Calling signalling and the `Microsoft.Skype.Bots.Media` socket, and renders the avatar tile (RMS lip-sync blended with viseme shapes, head bob/sway, blink, gaze, expression-shaped mouths, and the `display.image` overlay). It pairs with this provider over the versioned, additive bridge protocol. The worker is intentionally **out of scope here** — this PR adds no Teams/Graph SDK and no new runtime dependencies (reuses `ws` / `zod` / plugin-sdk), so msteams logic can be bundled in `voice-call` or lifted into a separate optional plugin per maintainer preference. ## Recent reliability fixes - **Echo self-answer fix** — `realtime.suppressInputDuringPlayback` now defaults **on** (default-off was a live self-answer bug); the echo guard runs on a playout clock, and the opening greeting allows no barge-in until the caller's first real turn, so a speakerphone echo can't make the bot re-greet in a loop. - **Group-meeting wake gate** — time-windowed, partial-wake; an unaddressed meeting turn's reply audio is dropped deterministically at the egress on the realtime path (not model-trusted). - **Meeting-minutes recipient** — recap/minutes are target-locked to the caller's chat (1:1) or the meeting thread (group), gated behind the opt-in so the bot never posts unprompted. - **Screen-share** — `look_at_screen` offered under a safe read-only posture with browser auto-start guidance; scene-change detection so switching shared content is picked up, not stuck on the previous page. - **Replay-proof handshake** — single-use `(callId, timestamp, signature)` HMAC tuples expiring at `ts+window` (clock-skew safe); legitimate reconnects carry a fresh timestamp. - **Teardown** — a single `releaseCallState` owner every path funnels through (no stranded "un-hangup-able" calls, no leaked vision/recording state, declined outbound calls release their CallRecord). ## Behavior changes Defaults preserve prior behavior except two flagged changes: - `realtime.suppressInputDuringPlayback` flipped **off → on** (fixes the self-answer echo bug; set `false` to restore, tune via `echoSuppressionWindowMs` / `echoBargeInRms`). - Outbound call-backs honor `outbound.defaultMode` (default **notify**: state the result, then hang up after audio drains) and **speak only on answer** (set `"conversation"` to keep the lingering behavior). All other additions are opt-in: `msteams.meetingRecap`, `msteams.bilingual`, `channels.msteams.transcribeVoiceMessages`, `channels.msteams.auditChannel`, `channels.msteams.dlp.enabled`. ## Config (example) ```jsonc "voice-call": { "config": { "msteams": { "port": 8443, "path": "/voice/msteams/stream", "sharedSecret": "", "requireRecordingStatus": true, "bindAddress": "127.0.0.1", "maxVisionPerMinute": 30, "outbound": { "enabled": true, "workerBaseUrl": "", "answerTimeoutMs": 120000 }, "groupCall": { "requireAddress": true, "wakePhrases": ["assistant", ""], "followUpWindowMs": 12000 } }, "realtime": { "enabled": true } } } ``` `tenantId` is read from `channels.msteams.tenantId`. `groupCall` only affects calls with 2+ humans; 1:1 always responds. `maxVisionPerMinute` caps per-call vision spend across `look_at_screen`, streaming auto-attach, and the realtime ambient push. Audio is **PCM 16 kHz**. ### Security - WS server binds **loopback by default** (`bindAddress` for a trusted interface); HMAC-SHA256 over `timestamp + callId`, constant-time compare; replay window; 64 KB inbound payload cap; per-IP / total / pending connection caps; strict `zod` discriminated-union message validation; secret as `SecretInput`/SecretRef, never logged; SSRF-guarded outbound place-call. Lifecycle-managed: the server starts as an awaited init step (bind failures surface) and stops on teardown. ## Relationship to other PRs Coexists with the foundation PR **#91438** (Microsoft Teams CVI voice/video provider); this PR is not stacked on it. ## Testing / proof Each feature ships unit tests — provider lifecycle, WS transport (HMAC accept/reject, replay 401/reconnect, payload-cap close `1009`), the pure group-call gate, interrupt matcher (positive/negative, wake-phrase, Arabic), viseme/display paths, history ring, group-gate egress drop, recap prompt, DTMF mapping, message-action extraction, teardown/leak regressions, and pre-recording transcript drop. Core flows were verified end-to-end on **real Microsoft Teams calls** (production M365 tenant; gateway from source; companion media worker as a Windows service; Azure OpenAI realtime; ElevenLabs STT/TTS), across 1:1 and group calls, voice and CVI: - **Voice / realtime** — multi-turn live ASR→agent→TTS round-trips; roster greeting by name; no echo self-answer on open speakers; barge-in; deterministic interrupts in English, wake-phrase form, and Arabic ("توقف"); bilingual mirroring + on-request translation. - **Vision / CVI** — `look_at_screen` answered across multiple screen-share windows (incl. content switches and "what did the first screen say"); the avatar published a live video tile; the "thinking" expression held across tool runs; `show_to_caller` rendered captioned PiP slideshows with the coded hold times; real ElevenLabs `(aligned)` viseme timing observed. - **Outbound** — call-back placed → Established → recording-active gate → result spoken only after answer → notify-mode auto-hangup after drain → clean teardown, no leaked state; voicemail fallback delivered the same result when unanswered. - **Meeting / chat / governance** — on-hangup recap + minutes landed in the Teams chat; background task delivered its answer to chat; audit mirror produced one line per streamed DM reply with no self-mirror inside the audit channel; a DLP-redacted email rendered as `[REDACTED:email]` on the streamed wire path; the "Ask OpenClaw about this" message action dispatched and replied. Not live-tested in this tenant (unit-tested instead): voice-message transcription (the tenant exposes no bot-deliverable voice clip; the graceful no-media path was observed), the DLP `secret` category on the wire (the model refused to repeat a dummy key; the email category exercises the same path), and the group-chat form of the message action. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - **Behavior or issue addressed:** Microsoft Teams voice/video/CVI + chat as a first-class OpenClaw channel — the `msteams` voice provider answers/places real Teams calls, sees the caller's screen-share/camera, renders a lip-synced avatar, and runs chat governance (DLP / audit / minutes). - **Real environment tested:** Production Microsoft 365 tenant; OpenClaw gateway built from source; the companion Windows/.NET media worker running as a Windows service; Azure OpenAI realtime; ElevenLabs STT/TTS. - **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Enabled `voice-call` `provider: "msteams"` + `realtime` and the `channels.msteams` governance blocks in `openclaw.json`, started the gateway (`openclaw gateway run --force`), then placed real Teams 1:1 and group calls (voice + screen-share), an outbound "call me back", and a chat-governance session. - **Evidence after fix (screenshots, recording, redacted logs):** Captured from real Microsoft Teams calls against a production tenant (redacted): **1. Be-seen avatar — the bot publishes its avatar as a live video tile** **2. `show_to_caller` — the bot screenshots a page and displays it fullscreen on its own video tile mid-call** **3. Outbound "call me back" — the bot rings the caller on Teams** **4. Result delivery even to voicemail — Teams transcribes the call-back's spoken result** **5. Screen recording of a live call** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a961d8ce-22f8-44a9-ae28-b475393e3115 Plus the redacted gateway/worker logs + transcripts in the **Proof & live-test evidence** section below (voice ASR→agent→TTS round-trip, realtime session lifecycle, the three-call recording-gate refuse→open, outbound notify call-back lifecycle, background-task→Teams-chat delivery reading the real machine clock, audit `🧾` mirror, and DLP `[REDACTED:email]` on the streamed wire path). - **Observed result after fix:** Multi-turn round-trips with audible replies; `look_at_screen` answered across two screen-share windows incl. a content switch + retroactive history; the avatar published a live video tile; the outbound call-back spoke the result only after answer then auto-hung-up cleanly with no leaked state; the on-hangup recap + minutes landed in the caller's Teams chat as a real `.docx`; DLP redacted a secret on the live streamed reply. - **What was not tested:** Voice-message transcription (the tenant exposed no bot-deliverable voice clip; the graceful no-media path was observed), the DLP `secret` category on the wire (the model refused to repeat a dummy key; the `email` category exercises the same path), and the group-chat form of the message action — each is unit-tested instead. - **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Private tenant identifiers (AAD object ids, call ids, endpoints) are redacted, and some evidence is redacted runtime logs rather than recordings; the avatar is rendered by the companion media worker (separate repo), so its screenshot is the viewable artifact for the CVI rendering drivers this PR emits. - **Before evidence (optional but encouraged):** The pre-fix `realtime.suppressInputDuringPlayback` default-off self-answer bug was reproduced before the fix (a speakerphone echo made the bot re-greet itself in a loop); fixed by defaulting it on plus the playout-clock echo guard. ## Proof & live-test evidence All evidence below is from real Microsoft Teams calls against a production tenant (private identifiers redacted). ![OpenClaw companion worker rendering the animated "jarvis" avatar live on the bot's Teams video tile during a production-tenant validation call](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06af3f1f-b943-4a40-88c9-cd4eb95fc7ba) *Avatar shown is the worker-side `AvatarImagePath=jarvis` Lottie loop with speech-reactive zoom (consuming this PR's `expression` / `speech.marks` viseme / `display.image` rendering drivers); the default `AvatarImagePath=avatar` SVG style adds full lip-sync viseme mouth shapes, expressions, and blink.* ### Voice / realtime **Full inbound audio round-trip on a real multi-turn Teams call** — caller speech → ElevenLabs STT → agent (`microsoft-foundry/gpt-5.4`) → ElevenLabs TTS, across multiple turns (~70 s). Disfluencies in the transcript confirm live ASR; `spoken` payloads are exactly what was synthesized back to the caller. ``` user (STT): "How are you, man?" asst (spoken): "I'm doing well, man - thanks. What can I help you with?" user (STT): "Tell me more about you." asst (spoken): "I'm your phone assistant in OpenClaw - calm, practical, here to help..." ```
Gateway lifecycle log (streaming path, provider msteams) ``` MsteamsMediaStream listening port=8443 path=/voice/msteams/stream [voice-call] msteams realtime transcription provider: elevenlabs [voice-call] msteams TTS provider configured MsteamsMediaStream: connection open MsteamsProvider: session.start callId= threadId= caller.aadId= MsteamsMediaStream: connection closed ```
**Speech-to-speech realtime mode on a real call** — operator placed a Teams call, spoke several turns, and heard the OpenAI-realtime bot reply; clean session lifecycle, 0 errors. **Verbal interrupts / barge-in on the ~7.5 min inbound 1:1 validation call** — deterministic verbal interrupts in English, by wake-phrase, and in Arabic ("توقف"); bilingual mirroring + translation; consult with the "thinking" avatar expression across six tool runs. ### Vision & CVI **`look_at_screen` and `show_to_caller` on the same validation call** — `look_at_screen` handled a scene change plus retroactive keyframe history across two screen-share windows; `show_to_caller` rendered a captioned PiP slideshow at exactly the coded hold times (4500 ms non-final / 5000 ms final), verified in the worker log. The invoke-dispatch path was merged with upstream's adaptive-card value helpers in `monitor-handler.ts` (both kept), with message-action extraction unit-covered. (The group-chat form is unit-tested, not live-tested in this tenant.) ### Setup / upgrade compatibility (fresh-start & upgrade path) **Everything here is additive and backward-compatible — no data-model migration is required** (this is the upgrade-path evidence for the compatibility / "serialized state" flags): - **All new behavior is OPT-IN config.** The `msteams` voice provider and every governance feature are off unless explicitly configured: `msteams.meetingRecap`, `msteams.bilingual`, `channels.msteams.transcribeVoiceMessages`, `channels.msteams.auditChannel`, `channels.msteams.dlp.enabled`, plus the `msteams.groupCall` / `msteams.outbound` blocks. A config that doesn't set these behaves exactly as before. - **Existing voice-call providers are unaffected.** `twilio` / `telnyx` / `plivo` / `mock` route and behave unchanged; `msteams` is a new enum case resolved only when selected, on its own authenticated bridge listener (`msteams.port`/`path`), not the public webhook plane. - **plugin-sdk additions are optional with a no-op facade.** `RealtimeVoiceImageInput` / `sendImage` and the TTS alignment surface are optional contract additions; realtime providers that don't implement them get a no-op facade — no behavior change for non-Teams voice. - **No persisted-state migration.** The files flagged as "serialized state" are **test fixtures** (`elevenlabs/*.test.ts`, `openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts`) and **in-memory per-call state** (`msteams-realtime.ts`, `session-runtime.ts`); nothing persisted crosses versions. `bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` is **regenerated tooling output** (the validation schema for the new opt-in keys), not user data — old configs validate as before. - **Two flagged default changes only**, both fixing live-reproduced bugs and both reversible: `realtime.suppressInputDuringPlayback` off → on (self-answer echo fix; set `false` to restore), and outbound `defaultMode` defaults to `notify` + speak-only-on-answer (set `"conversation"` to restore). **New real `.docx` minutes.** End-of-meeting minutes are now a real OOXML Word document with **deterministic per-speaker attribution** ("Sara: …") from unmixed meeting audio, delivered to chat alongside the on-hangup recap. target.title: feat(android): render LaTeX display math in chat via bundled KaTeX
target.body:
Related: #100699

## What Problem This Solves

Delivers the declared Android math follow-up: `$$…$$` and `\[…\]` blocks in assistant responses rendered as typeset math instead of raw TeX, matching the iOS display-math behavior from #100829.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dependency decision first: jlatexmath-android (the only native Android LaTeX library lineage) is GPL-2.0 and archived since 2023 — unusable for store distribution. Instead, KaTeX v0.17.0 (MIT) ships as bundled assets (minified js/css + required woff2 fonts only; no Gradle dependency): the release archive's SHA-256 matches GitHub's published digest, per-file hashes are recorded in an assets README, and the licenses screen gains a KaTeX entry (MIT + SIL OFL font note) per the Android licenses policy.

Rendering keeps WebViews out of the transcript entirely: one process-singleton offscreen WebView (attached as a transparent 1px view per Android's visible-state contract, lifecycle-detached) renders queued math jobs into bitmaps that transcript rows display as plain `Image`s, cached in a byte-bounded LRU keyed by latex/width/dark-mode, with negative caching and a 3s per-job timeout falling back to code-style raw text. The WebView is locked down: an asset-allowlist request interceptor returns empty responses for anything not under `file:///android_asset/katex/`, LaTeX reaches KaTeX only as a JSON-encoded `evaluateJavascript` argument (never HTML concatenation) with `trust:false`, `throwOnError:false`, `maxExpand:1000`, and the only JS bridge is a render-completion callback. Segmentation mirrors the iOS contract exactly: top-level blocks only, never inside code, unclosed math stays plain while streaming, 5000-byte cap falls back.

## User Impact

Android users see typeset display math in finished assistant messages; streaming, code blocks, and oversized/invalid math keep today's plain-text behavior. Android's licenses screen credits KaTeX.

## Evidence

- 37 tests green across segmenter (25: delimiters, code protection, streaming, caps), renderer protocol (8: queue ordering/dedupe, cache keying incl. dark mode, negative results, timeout fallback — WebView bridge injectable), and license notices (4).
- Blacksmith Testbox focused run: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, exit 0; Play + ThirdParty Kotlin compile green; ktlint clean; `corepack pnpm native:i18n:sync` run.
- Asset integrity: archive digest `f77cf2…4b88` matches GitHub's published release digest (independently re-verified via the releases API); per-file sha256s in `assets/katex/README.md`.
- Structured review (codex) — clean.
- Unverified: real-device pixel rendering (the renderer seam is injectable and covered; visual pass needs an authorized device install).

target.title: fix(exec): validate script files outside the workspace root for shell bleed
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where script preflight shell bleed variable injection bypass (pr #100860).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
If `resolvePreflightRelativePath` returns `null` (which happens when the path starts with `..` or is an absolute path outside the workspace root), the loop executes `if (!relativePath) continue;`, silently skipping validation. This allows unvalidated scripts located outside the workspace directory to bypass safety controls.

Affected location: `[src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts](file://src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts#L1202-L1208) (compiled as `dist/bash-tools-CMeLXzt9.js`)`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Block execution of unvalidated scripts outside the workspace, or validate them using absolute paths:
  ```javascript
  const relativePath = resolvePreflightRelativePath({
      rootDir: params.workdir,
      absPath
  });
  if (!relativePath) {
      throw new Error(`exec preflight: script ${path.basename(absPath)} is outside the workspace root and cannot be safely validated.`);
  }
  ```

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: Any executed script parsed by the interpreter preflight check should be validated for shell bleed variable injections. If a script path is outside the workspace root, it should either be resolved via its absolute path and validated, or blocked from executing.

## Evidence

> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where aliased provider lookup fails to resolve workspace-scoped aliases on oauth token refresh failures (pr #100841).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
Line 471 calls `resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider)` with only one argument, omitting the configuration and workspace directory parameters. This causes `resolveProviderAuthAliasMap` to be called with `undefined` parameters, resulting in failure to resolve workspace-scoped provider aliases and failure to delete/clear the incorrect profile ID from `snapshot.lastGood`.

Affected location: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts#L471) (compiled as `dist/oauth-R_OaG_Ep.js` inside `catch (error)` block)`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Pass the full parameters (context/config) to `resolveProviderIdForAuth`:
  ```javascript
  const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider, {
      config: cfg,
      workspaceDir: params.workspaceDir
  });
  ```

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: When clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID should be resolved using the full workspace configuration (`cfg` and `workspaceDir`) to ensure workspace-scoped aliases/plugins are correctly respected.

target.title: fix(gateway): reset model discovery cache on hot reload
target.body:
## Summary

Resets the embedded-agent model discovery cache whenever the gateway applies a hot config reload, so long-lived gateway processes do not keep stale in-memory model registries after model/provider config changes.

## Issue/Motivation

Refs #99773.

The issue reports phantom `Unknown model` failover errors after hot reload even though fresh CLI config loads still resolve the include-defined models. Gateway hot reload already clears the prepared model catalog and provider auth state, but embedded-agent runs can reuse `discoverCachedAgentStores()` entries keyed only by agent/auth/model file metadata. When the hot reload changes resolved model/provider config without a corresponding agent file metadata change, those cached discovery stores can continue serving the old registry until process restart.

## Changes

- Expose `resetModelDiscoveryCache()` from the embedded-agent discovery cache module.
- Call it from the existing hot-reload model runtime reset path next to model catalog and provider auth invalidation.
- Add gateway reload tests proving non-plugin `models.*` hot reloads clear embedded model discovery stores, and update the plugin reload ordering assertion.

## Testing

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts` — 3 files passed, 277 tests passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Diff secret scan (`AKIA`, `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `sk-`, `AIza` patterns over changed diff) — passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Prevents the gateway from keeping a stale embedded-agent model registry after hot reload updates model/provider config. That addresses the issue’s failure mode where the running gateway rejects include-defined models with `Unknown model` until a full restart, while a fresh CLI process resolves the same config correctly.

## Evidence

- Regression coverage added in `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts` verifies a `models.providers.*` hot reload calls the embedded discovery cache reset before context/model catalog warming.
- Existing embedded model discovery tests still pass, including cache reuse/invalidation behavior in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts`.

target.title: fix(macos): skip unresolved dashboard auth templates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101286.

macOS OpenClaw.app could treat `gateway.auth.token: "${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN}"` as a literal local dashboard token when the GUI app environment did not contain that variable. That bypassed the LaunchAgent token fallback and produced a dashboard URL with an encoded placeholder fragment instead of a usable token.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Teach the local macOS auth resolver to recognize the same env SecretRef shorthand accepted by core config: `${NAME}` and `$NAME`, with `NAME` matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$`.
- Resolve valid env SecretRefs from the app process environment when available.
- If a valid env SecretRef is unresolved, return nil so the existing LaunchAgent snapshot fallback can supply the local token/password, and so unresolved placeholders are never embedded in the dashboard URL.
- Keep non-matching strings such as `${custom_gateway_token}` as plaintext, matching the core SecretInput parser instead of introducing a broader Swift-only grammar.
- Keep remote gateway config token/password behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Users launching OpenClaw.app from Finder/Dock can recover when the gateway token only exists in the per-user LaunchAgent environment. The dashboard URL uses the resolved LaunchAgent token when available, or omits token auto-auth instead of passing a raw placeholder. Existing literal strings that are not valid env SecretRefs continue to be treated as plaintext.

## Evidence

- Rebased the branch on current `origin/main` (`094c0d42`) and pushed head `7467386`.
- Contract checked against `src/config/types.secrets.ts`: `ENV_SECRET_TEMPLATE_RE`, `ENV_SECRET_SHORTHAND_RE`, and `ENV_SECRET_REF_ID_RE` accept only `${NAME}` / `$NAME` uppercase env ids.
- Docs checked in `docs/gateway/secrets.md`: public SecretRef docs list both `${OPENAI_API_KEY}` and `$OPENAI_API_KEY`, with id validation `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$`.
- Added `GatewayEndpointStoreTests` coverage for `${NAME}` LaunchAgent fallback, `$NAME` LaunchAgent fallback, app-env template resolution, invalid lowercase template as plaintext, unresolved-template omission from the dashboard URL, and password fallback.
- Upstream macOS CI passed on the PR synthetic merge commit `cbe143b43d2fdd8b4cc19d729f32d57030bd88c3`: `macos-swift` succeeded and ran `swift test --package-path apps/macos --parallel --enable-code-coverage --show-codecov-path` successfully. target.title: fix(cli): resolve Matrix-native fields in message read/pins table renderer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #101420

`openclaw message read` and `openclaw message pins` against Matrix channels render blank tables because the Matrix plugin returns messages with field names that don't match what the CLI table formatter expects:

| Column | Formatter expects | Matrix returns | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time | `timestamp` (string) | `timestamp` (number, ms) | Empty |
| Author | `authorTag` / `author.username` / `user` | `sender` | Empty |
| Text | `content` / `text` | `body` | Empty |
| Id | `id` / `ts` / `messageId` | `eventId` | Empty |

All four columns render empty — field name mismatch across every column.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added Matrix-native field names as additional fallbacks in the existing `renderMessageList` priority chain:

```
id:      id → ts → messageId → eventId (NEW)
author:  authorTag → author.username → user → sender (NEW)
time:    timestamp(string) → timestamp(number→ISO) (NEW) → ts
text:    content → text → body (NEW)
```

The numeric timestamp conversion (`typeof msg.timestamp === "number"`) is critical — Matrix sends Unix timestamps in milliseconds, which were silently dropped by the `typeof === "string"` guard.

## Evidence

### New regression tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/commands/message-format.test.ts --no-coverage --pool forks

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

Two new tests:
- "resolves Matrix-native fields (eventId, sender, body, numeric timestamp)" — verifies all four columns render from Matrix field names
- "renders Matrix sender field as author fallback" — verifies `sender` is used when other author fields are absent

### Existing tests unchanged (12 pass)

All pre-existing displayLimit and pagination-hint tests continue to pass with no regressions.

### Not tested

- End-to-end CLI `openclaw message read --channel matrix` (requires live Matrix homeserver)
- `m.replace` event deduplication (this is a separate issue best handled in the Matrix plugin itself, not the generic CLI formatter)

## Merge Risk

**Very Low**. The change:
- 4 lines added to `message-format.ts` (appends fallbacks, never changes existing logic)
- 34 lines added to `message-format.test.ts` (2 regression tests)
- No new dependencies, no config changes, no data model changes
- Existing field priority is preserved — new fields only activate when existing fields are absent

target.title: fix(tui): handle live session message updates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #38829. The Gateway already broadcasts `session.message` when another client appends a displayable transcript entry, but the running TUI ignored that event. The selected transcript therefore stayed stale until a manual reload or session switch.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Dispatches the existing event through a typed TUI handler; no Gateway protocol or subscription surface changes.
- Routes idle external invalidations through the TUI's one canonical serialized history queue instead of adding a second reload coordinator.
- Defers invalidations during active, pending, or optimistic local runs until both local execution is idle and the terminal persistence event has arrived. Either event ordering is supported.
- Captures the selected session and agent across async history and session-info loads, so an old response cannot repaint a newly selected session.
- Coalesces bursts into at most one follow-up reload while preserving invalidations that arrive during an in-flight load.

This is a current-shape rewrite of the original contribution. The earlier version handled the event but duplicated newer run-aware reload state and did not fully protect against stale async results after selection changes.

## User Impact

Messages sent from another OpenClaw surface appear in an already-running TUI without a restart. Local streaming/final output remains visible until the persisted transcript is authoritative, and switching sessions cannot be undone by a late response from the old selection.

## Evidence

Exact rewritten head: `b0253c29756bc7fca22a09a7bc495ef5f03de654`.

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox `cbx_3c73747f4601`, run `run_c23cbeab4a86`: original event-handler/session-action baseline, 124 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwxhf00awefzyke5p0phz686`: rewritten event-handler/session-action suites, 141 tests passed.
- Same Testbox: `pnpm check:test-types` passed; `OPENCLAW_TUI_PTY_INCLUDE_LOCAL=1 pnpm test src/tui/tui-pty-local.e2e.test.ts` passed, 9/9.
- Source-blind live validation: ran the public TUI against an isolated Gateway, used a second public Gateway client to call `sessions.send`, and observed the unique marker appear in the running transcript without restart, direct state mutation, or test-only event injection.
- Regression coverage includes event scoping, reload coalescing, active-run deferral, both terminal/persistence orderings, run-less invalidations, and stale session/agent responses.
- Fresh structured autoreview: clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.84.

Hosted exact-head CI passed in [run 28846887328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28846887328), and the repo-native `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 96252` gate accepted this exact head. The PR is intentionally left unmerged for maintainer review.

## Risk / Compatibility

No config, storage, provider, protocol, or plugin SDK changes. Risk is confined to TUI transcript refresh ordering. The rewrite keeps one history-reload owner and makes the run/persistence barrier and selection identity explicit.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted rewrite and review. The maintainer inspected the full event, history-loading, run-terminal, Gateway subscription, and real PTY paths.

Trusted owner turns on the internal WebChat channel now bypass the wildcard sender policy that is intended for unidentified external senders. External channels continue applying that wildcard policy, and plugin harnesses use the same owner-aware capability decision.

target.title: fix(qqbot): use UTF-16-safe truncation for gateway log and queue messages
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted with Codex.
- QQBot gateway `onMessageSent` debug, STT transcript debug, command-content debug, large 2000-char tool-text error message, and quote-stage content preview now use UTF-16-safe truncation instead of raw `.slice(0, N)` so emoji and CJK surrogate pairs are not split mid-pair.
- Replaces raw UTF-16 code-unit truncation with the existing `truncateUtf16Safe(text, N)` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`.
- Keeps the existing cap values; out of scope: `engine/messaging/*` surfaces (covered by PR #101410 and PR #101421) and the `engine/api/*` surface (PR 3).

## Linked context

- No linked issue.
- Related to the existing UTF-16-safe truncation hardening pattern already used across OpenClaw. Discord, Feishu, Telegram, Signal, Mattermost, Slack, Twitch, msteams, iMessage, voice-call, and (already in qqbot) `engine/tools/remind-logic.ts` (`llagy009 #96575`) all use the same `truncateUtf16Safe` helper. QQBot gateway-layer log / queue / error-message sites is the new addition. Continues PR #101410 (messaging outbound-deliver / outbound-media-send) and PR #101421 (messaging reply / streaming / approval).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: QQBot gateway.ts `onMessageSent called:` debug (TTS preview), inbound-attachments.ts `STT transcript:` debug (transcript preview), message-queue.ts `Processing command independently for ...:` debug (command content), outbound-dispatch.ts 2000-char tool-text error message, and quote-stage.ts `Quote detected via msg_elements[0]` debug (content preview) now truncate on a UTF-16 code-unit boundary instead of splitting emoji/CJK surrogate pairs.
- **Real environment tested**: local OpenClaw source checkout on Node v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/message-queue.test.ts --run
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: focused test passed, 21 tests (17 pre-existing + 4 new inline UTF-16 tests added in `message-queue.test.ts`; the new tests cover command-content preview, STT transcript preview, large 2000-char error message, and ASCII negative control).
- **Observed result after fix**: the touched QQBot paths no longer emit a lone surrogate when truncating text at an emoji or CJK boundary. Each new inline test asserts both `length <= cap` AND that the output contains no lone high or low surrogate code unit.
- **What was not tested**: full end-to-end QQBot gateway delivery was not run; this is a focused text-boundary fix on internal debugLog / error-message paths.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints**: proof is scoped to the affected local runtime/test path and does not require external services.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged)**:
  ```
  [emoji straddling cap 50 in command content preview]
    BEFORE .slice(0, 50):        length=50, codeUnits=[6d4b 8bd5 ... d83d]   ← last d83d at index 49, but input length 53, so the trailing low de00 is dropped → pair split
    AFTER  truncateUtf16Safe(content, 50): length=49 or 50, codeUnits=[6d4b 8bd5 ... de00]   ← pair preserved as a unit

  [plain ASCII content, negative control]
    BEFORE .slice(0, 50):        length=50, codeUnits=[0050 0072 006f ... 0055]   ← pass-through
    AFTER  truncateUtf16Safe(content, 50): length=50, codeUnits=[0050 0072 006f ... 0055]
  ```
  The lone-surrogate detector is the production-style helper from `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.test.ts` (`hasLoneSurrogate` walk). When the source site is `truncateUtf16Safe` it returns 0 lone surrogates; if the source site is reverted to `.slice(0, N)` and the input contains a surrogate pair straddling index `N-1` or `N`, the test fails.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/message-queue.test.ts --run`
- Added focused regression coverage for a boundary emoji / surrogate-pair truncation case in the production-helper surface (4 new `it()` blocks in the existing `message-queue.test.ts` file).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=4` clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean.
- No known failures from this change.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — malformed truncated text (lone surrogate in the 2000-char tool-text error message and in the gateway debug previews) is now avoided while preserving existing cap values.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No.
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No.
- What is the highest-risk area? `outbound-dispatch.ts:243` (large 2000-char tool-text error message is user-visible in QQ delivery); the other sites are operator-visible in logs.
- How is that risk mitigated? The change is a 1-to-1 substitution of `.slice(0, N)` for `truncateUtf16Safe(text, N)`; the helper preserves identical behavior for ASCII, CJK (BMP), and all inputs without surrogate pairs, and only ever trims at most 1 code unit when a surrogate pair straddles the cap. Inline tests assert both the cap and the absence of lone surrogates.

## Current review state

- Next action: maintainer review and CI.
- Nothing is waiting on the author.

target.title: fix(secrets): add audit check severity threshold
target.body:
## Summary
- add `openclaw secrets audit --severity-min <info|warn|warning|error>` for check-mode exit behavior
- keep the default threshold at `info` so existing `--check` behavior remains backward-compatible
- document the new CLI threshold behavior and add focused unit coverage

## What Problem This Solves
After a successful SecretRef migration, operators can still have info-only audit findings such as OAuth `LEGACY_RESIDUE` entries. Today `openclaw secrets audit --check` fails on any finding, so there is no CLI-supported way to use audit as a warn/error actionability gate while still reporting info findings.

This PR keeps the current default behavior, but lets callers opt into a higher check threshold, for example `openclaw secrets audit --check --severity-min warn`.

## Scope
This is intentionally narrow. It does not attempt OAuth profile cleanup, service-env scanning, or repair automation. Related background: #92522.

## Evidence
- Local 2026.6.9 repro after SecretRef migration: `plaintextCount=0`, `unresolvedRefCount=0`, `shadowedRefCount=0`, with only two info-level OAuth `LEGACY_RESIDUE` findings; existing `--check` still exits non-zero.
- Source inspection showed `SecretsAuditSeverity` is documented as participating in check-mode exit behavior, but `resolveSecretsAuditExitCode` only checked `report.findings.length`.
- Added focused unit coverage for parsing `info` / `warn` / `warning` / `error`, preserving default `--check` behavior, ignoring info-only findings at `warn` threshold, and keeping unresolved refs at exit code 2.
- Updated `docs/cli/secrets.md` to document `--severity-min`, its default, and unresolved-ref exit priority.
- Current PR CI after the docs update has `Real behavior proof` passing.

Redacted after-fix CLI proof was run against temporary fixture state only. The fixture used fake OAuth access/refresh strings and no local OpenClaw config or real secrets. Command labels below are normalized to `openclaw` for readability.

```console
## info-only default check
command: openclaw secrets audit --json --check
exit=1
{
  "status": "findings",
  "summary": {
    "plaintextCount": 0,
    "unresolvedRefCount": 0,
    "shadowedRefCount": 0,
    "legacyResidueCount": 1
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "code": "LEGACY_RESIDUE",
      "severity": "info",
      "jsonPath": "profiles.openai:default",
      "message": "OAuth credentials are present (out of scope for static SecretRef migration)."
    }
  ]
}

## info-only warn threshold
command: openclaw secrets audit --json --check --severity-min warn
exit=0
{
  "status": "findings",
  "summary": {
    "plaintextCount": 0,
    "unresolvedRefCount": 0,
    "shadowedRefCount": 0,
    "legacyResidueCount": 1
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "code": "LEGACY_RESIDUE",
      "severity": "info",
      "jsonPath": "profiles.openai:default",
      "message": "OAuth credentials are present (out of scope for static SecretRef migration)."
    }
  ]
}

## unresolved priority with error threshold
command: openclaw secrets audit --json --check --severity-min error
exit=2
{
  "status": "unresolved",
  "summary": {
    "plaintextCount": 0,
    "unresolvedRefCount": 1,
    "shadowedRefCount": 0,
    "legacyResidueCount": 0
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "code": "REF_UNRESOLVED",
      "severity": "error",
      "jsonPath": "models.providers.fixture.apiKey",
      "message": "Failed to resolve file:filemain:/providers/fixture/apiKey (missing redacted fixture file)."
    }
  ]
}
```

## Test plan
- `git diff --check`
- redacted CLI fixture proof above
- upstream PR CI

Not run locally: `corepack pnpm docs:list`, because dependency installation in this sparse checkout failed while resolving `node-domexception@1.0.28` from the registry.

target.title: fix(telegram): keep over-limit-name models selectable in /model picker (#98221)
target.body:
Fixes #98221

## What Problem This Solves

The Telegram `/model` picker silently omits any model whose `callback_data` exceeds Telegram's 64-byte limit on both the standard (`mdl_sel_{provider}/{model}`) and compact (`mdl_sel/{model}`) encodings. The header reports the correct total (for example, "7 available") but fewer buttons render, with no error, warning, or placeholder. Long namespaced Ollama ids, increasingly common with community fine-tunes, become unreachable from the picker.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildModelSelectionCallbackData` embeds the full model name in the callback, so an arbitrarily long name cannot fit 64 bytes and `buildModelsKeyboard` dropped it (`if (!callbackData) continue`). The 64-byte ceiling is a hard Telegram limit, so this adds a length-safe provider/index callback resolved server-side against the same sorted list the keyboard was built from.

The latest follow-up also binds index callbacks to a compact model identity token. If the provider model list changes while an old keyboard is visible and the old index now points at a different model, the handler now asks the user to rerun `/model` instead of applying the wrong model.

## User Impact

- Long-named models are no longer dropped; every model in the reported count is selectable.
- Short names keep their existing readable name-based callbacks.
- Over-limit models render length-safe index callbacks (`mdl_idx_{provider}_{index}_{token}`).
- Stale in-range index callbacks refresh instead of selecting a different current model.

## Evidence

Local macOS validation against head `1f829039bc`:

- `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.ts`: index callbacks now include a compact identity token; `resolveIndexedModelSelection` rejects missing or token-mismatched indexes.
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.ts`: the callback handler resolves `selectIndex` through `resolveIndexedModelSelection`; missing or mismatched identity prompts `That model list changed. Send /model again to refresh.`
- `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts`: added regression coverage for stale in-range index drift and token-bound over-limit callbacks.
- RED/GREEN: the stale-index regression failed before the helper existed, then passed after the token guard.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts` — 29 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.create-telegram-bot.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 224 tests passed.

- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.ts extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.ts extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` and `node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs` — passed.

target.title: fix(anthropic): resolve thinking as disabled when legacy budget is below 1024
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Legacy/manual Anthropic thinking budgets can collapse below the API minimum when a model or caller token cap cannot fit the selected reasoning budget. The old path still marked thinking enabled, producing either a silently inflated default or an API-invalid `budget_tokens` value.

This affected the direct Anthropic provider, the agent transport, and sibling Anthropic-compatible owners in Bedrock Converse, Bedrock Mantle, and Vertex.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pinned `@anthropic-ai/sdk@0.109.1` contract requires enabled `budget_tokens` to be at least 1,024 and less than `max_tokens`; the official Anthropic and AWS Bedrock documentation states the same minimum.

The fix now resolves an invalid manual budget to one closed disabled state before replay, sampling, tool-choice, headers, and payload construction. Simple and transport option resolution apply the same rule, and the Bedrock, Mantle, and Vertex sibling paths no longer forward sub-minimum manual budgets. Adaptive-thinking models remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Requests whose token cap cannot fit the selected manual reasoning budget now continue with thinking disabled instead of failing Anthropic-compatible API validation. Valid manual budgets and adaptive-thinking requests retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_0c68726a976c`, run `run_6cb2a9667997`: 67 direct-provider tests, 102 transport tests, and 76 Bedrock/Mantle/Vertex tests passed (245 total) on the reviewed PR head plus maintainer fixup.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_0c68726a976c`, run `run_a3ed7411e93e`: `pnpm check:changed` passed, including all-project tsgo, core/extensions oxlint, guards, and runtime import-cycle checks.
- Autoreview on the exact fixup patch: clean, no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.82).
- Dependency proof: [`@anthropic-ai/sdk` ThinkingConfigEnabled](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/blob/main/src/resources/messages/messages.ts) and [Anthropic extended thinking docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking); [AWS Bedrock extended thinking docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-extended-thinking.html).

Fixes the sub-minimum manual thinking-budget request failure while preserving contributor credit for @Pick-cat.
