target.title: fix: show exported tool results in trace viewers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes tool results being invisible in LLM trace viewers that consume the OTel GenAI semantic conventions. Local Phoenix traces showed tool-result message cards with no visible output, and tool execution spans exposed captured tool I/O only under OpenClaw-private attribute names.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: the exporter emitted `tool_call_response` message parts keyed `result`, but the OTel GenAI semconv JSON Schema (`docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-input-messages.json`, unchanged since its introduction in v1.37) requires that field to be named `response`. Schema-validating viewers fail the typed part match and silently drop the part — Phoenix's gen_ai-to-OpenInference converter (pydantic models generated from that schema) renders an empty tool card, which is exactly the reported symptom.

- `tool_call_response` parts in `gen_ai.input.messages`/`gen_ai.output.messages` now emit the semconv `response` key (loose producer keys `result`/`content`/`details` are still accepted on input). Pure-text part arrays are flattened into one readable string (with a disclosed `...(N more text parts omitted)` marker past the array cap); mixed/structured results keep their raw (bounded, redacted) shape.
- Tool execution spans now carry the semconv execute_tool identity: `gen_ai.operation.name=execute_tool` (the Required classifier semconv-aware backends key on) and `gen_ai.tool.call.id`, and mirror explicitly captured tool inputs/results to `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`/`gen_ai.tool.call.result` (still gated by `diagnostics.otel.captureContent.toolInputs`/`toolOutputs`, normalized once and byte-identical to the shipped `openclaw.content.tool_*` names).

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Operators inspecting future OpenClaw traces see captured tool results in Phoenix chat views (`message.tool_call_id` + `message.content` derived from the `tool_call_response` part) and in standard GenAI tool span views (Langfuse/Opik map `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`/`result` to observation input/output). Existing traces are not rewritten. `openclaw.content.*` remain the stable OpenClaw attribute names; the `gen_ai.*` copies mirror them for semconv-native viewers.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox unit suite: `pnpm test extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts` — 106/106 passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox live E2E (lease `golden-lobster`): real gateway + `diagnostics-otel` + `captureContent` enabled, OTLP/http-protobuf to an otelcol-contrib 0.155.0 fan-out (file exporter + forward to a real Phoenix 17.20.0), one-shot `openclaw agent` turn on `xai/grok-4.3` that invoked the `read` tool:
  - Wire (collector file exporter): tool span carries `gen_ai.operation.name=execute_tool`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`, `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments={"path":...}`, `gen_ai.tool.call.result` byte-identical to `openclaw.content.tool_output`; the tool message part exported as `{type:"tool_call_response", id, response:"otel-e2e-proof-7431: ..."}` — 1 `response` key, 0 legacy `result` keys across all exported messages.
  - Phoenix (queried via client API): tool span converted to `span_kind=TOOL` with `tool.id`/`tool.name`/`tool.parameters`/`output.value` populated, and the LLM span's `llm.input_messages` contains `{"message.role":"tool","message.tool_call_id":"...","message.content":"otel-e2e-proof-7431: semconv response key smoke\n"}` — the previously-empty tool card now renders its content.
- `oxfmt --check --threads=1` on both changed TS files; `git diff --check` clean.
- Dependency contract proof (read from source):
  - OTel semconv `gen-ai-input-messages.json` at v1.37.0 and v1.41.0: `ToolCallResponsePart` `required: ["type", "response"]` — `result` was never the schema key. The three new span attributes use the `ATTR_GEN_AI_TOOL_CALL_*` constants from the pinned `@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions@1.41.1`.
  - Phoenix `src/phoenix/trace/gen_ai/conversion.py` `_flatten_message`: maps part `id` → `message.tool_call_id` and part `response` → `message.content`; parts keyed `result` fail the generated pydantic model (`response` required) and are silently dropped as `GenericPart`.
  - Langfuse `packages/shared/src/server/otel/OtelIngestionProcessor.ts`: presence-based fallback maps `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`/`gen_ai.tool.call.result` → observation input/output.
  - Opik `apps/opik-backend/.../otel/GenAIMappingRules.java`: same tool-span input/output mapping.

target.title: fix(ports): ignore malformed lsof listener pids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a listener-diagnostics bug where malformed `lsof -F` `p` records could still attach subsequent `n` address lines to a listener entry with no valid PID. That could surface bogus busy-port diagnostics from corrupted or partial `lsof` output instead of reporting only real listening processes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ports-inspect.ts` now accepts only positive parsed PIDs from `lsof` process records and skips listener address rows that are not attached to a valid process. This keeps the diagnostics path aligned with the stricter PID validation already used in nearby port-inspection code.

## User Impact

Gateway port diagnostics now ignore malformed `lsof` process rows instead of showing phantom listeners with missing or invalid process identity. Valid listener output is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests
Fresh focused test runs on commit 16369d50 (after the latest manual `main` merge into this branch):

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ports.test.ts src/cli/program.force.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Start at  09:35:28
   Duration  1.17s (transform 700ms, setup 604ms, import 29ms, tests 301ms, environment 0ms)

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
   Start at  09:35:35
   Duration  1.17s (transform 678ms, setup 491ms, import 192ms, tests 161ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 19.99s
```

Coverage called out by Codex is present on the current branch head:
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` keeps the repeated-listener dedupe test
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` rejects malformed diagnostics tokens like `p111abc`
- `src/cli/program.force.test.ts` rejects malformed force-free tokens like `p111abc`

### Real Behavior Proof (for ClawSweeper/Codex)

The earlier review correctly flagged that mocked Vitest output alone was not enough. Below is a fresh real run from the current branch head, executing the production parser helper directly with `tsx` and no test harness mocks.

```bash
$ node --import tsx ./tmp-pid-proof.mjs
=== Real production code execution (no mocks) ===
Legacy behavior:  Number.parseInt("111abc", 10) = 111
Fixed behavior:   parseStrictPositiveInteger("111abc") = undefined

Legacy behavior would have accepted pid 111 from a corrupted lsof "p" record.
Fixed behavior correctly returns undefined so the record is dropped.
```

The code path now used by diagnostics is `src/infra/ports-inspect.ts:53-56`:

```typescript
if (line.startsWith("p")) {
  const pid = parseStrictPositiveInteger(line.slice(1));
  processFields = pid !== undefined ? { pid } : {};
}
```

The sibling force-free parser is hardened the same way in `src/cli/ports.ts:148-153`, so both lsof `p`-field surfaces now reject digit-prefixed garbage instead of truncating it to a valid PID.

**Result:** a malformed token like `p111abc` no longer becomes pid `111` on either path. Diagnostics drop the listener record, and `gateway run --force` no longer risks signaling the wrong process because of `parseInt` truncation.

**Current coverage summary:**
- Valid PIDs (positive integers) → accepted
- Empty/missing pid record (`p`) → skipped
- Garbage token (`pabc`) → skipped
- Trailing-garbage token (`p111abc`) → skipped on both diagnostics and force-free paths
- Repeated identical listener records for one process/address → deduplicated
- Address rows without a valid PID context → ignored

target.title: refactor(codex): keyed turn routing, client-scoped rate limits, and resume subscription safety
target.body:
Closes #101338
Related: #93313

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a Codex usage-limit failure could report another account's rate-limit reset time and block the wrong auth profile: the rate-limit cache was process-global, so snapshots observed by one physical app-server client leaked into usage-limit errors on a different client. It also replaces the broad per-attempt notification/request fanout that made every attempt see and re-filter all app-server traffic, let `thread/resume` adopt mismatched or indeterminate subscriptions on pooled clients, and reinstalled auth-refresh handlers per attempt/side-question instead of per client.

## Why This Change Was Made

Re-implements the turn-routing and client-runtime-ownership track of #93313 on current `main` (that branch is thousands of commits behind and cannot be rebased). One turn router per physical client owns explicit per-thread routes with a reserve → arm → bind lifecycle: startup reserves the route before `thread/resume` so early notifications buffer instead of racing, `turn/start` arms the route, and binding the accepted turn id flushes buffered traffic in wire order. Rate limits move to a `WeakMap` keyed by the physical client with per-`limitId` revisions, merging rolling `account/rateLimits/updated` payloads per the protocol's sparse-update contract; usage-limit errors only trust a snapshot for profile blocking when the same client observed a primary update during the failing turn's startup. `thread/resume` moves into a dedicated module that retires the exact client when acceptance is indeterminate (only a structured RPC rejection proves no subscription). The positional-arg `client-factory.ts` indirection is deleted. Out of scope, tracked in #101338: the #93313 native-subagent-monitor status-revision rework and its compact generalization (main has since shipped a newer compaction completion-watch design).

## User Impact

Usage-limit errors now report the reset time for the account that actually hit the limit, and auth-profile blocking can no longer be triggered by another client's rate-limit traffic. Turn traffic on shared Codex app-server processes is routed per thread/turn, and a resume that Codex did not provably accept can no longer return a subscribed client to the shared pool. No config or API surface changes.

## Evidence

- Codex protocol contracts verified against the vendored `@openai/codex` 0.142.5 generated schemas and upstream `codex-rs` source (sparse rolling rate-limit updates, `willRetry` camelCase, top-level `threadId` on turn-scoped notifications, `thread/unsubscribe` status semantics).
- Full `extensions/codex` suite green on Blacksmith Testbox (95 files / 1985 tests; final rerun in PR checks).
- `pnpm check:changed` green on Blacksmith Testbox (typecheck extensions + tests, oxlint, guards): Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28841817056.
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.5) ran to clean over three cycles; accepted findings (resume fallback gating, idle-clock rewind clamp, `will_retry` alias removal) are fixed with regression tests. New regression coverage: cross-limit rate-limit trust, resume echo/mismatch retirement, rejected-resume unsubscribe fallback, keyed-router unit suite (940-line `turn-router.test.ts`).

target.title: fix(imessage): handle CLI child stdout/stderr stream errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runIMessageCliJson` in both `actions.runtime.ts` and `send.ts` spawned an `imsg` child process and listened for `data`, child `error`, and `close` events, but it did not attach `error` listeners to the piped `stdout` and `stderr` streams. If either stream emitted an error (for example, a broken pipe or EPIPE while the child was terminating), the error became an unhandled stream error and could crash the gateway worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node Readable streams can emit `error` independently of the child process `error` event. For transport code that runs inside the gateway process, unhandled stream errors are a reliability risk. Adding explicit `error` handlers on both `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` lets the promise reject cleanly and gives operators a concrete error message instead of an unhandled exception.

## User Impact

- iMessage CLI sends and actions now fail gracefully when the child's stdout or stderr stream errors.
- The gateway no longer risks an unhandled stream exception from `imsg` child I/O.
- Existing success paths and timeout/kill escalation behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added `error` event handlers to `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` in both `extensions/imessage/src/actions.runtime.ts` and `extensions/imessage/src/send.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `extensions/imessage/src/actions.runtime.test.ts` and `extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts` covering stdout and stderr stream errors.
- Local test runs:

  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/imessage/src/actions.runtime.test.ts --run  # 21 tests passed

target.title: fix(whatsapp): suppress unhandled rejections from void fire-and-forget calls
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** Four fire-and-forget `void` async calls in the WhatsApp extension could produce unhandled Promise rejections when their underlying asynchronous operations failed, which would crash the gateway.

**Solution:** Each call now uses `.catch()` to absorb the rejection. All four paths are best-effort: `logSelfId` is periodic status logging, and status reactions are non-critical lifecycle signaling.

**What changed:** +2 lines of `.catch()` handlers at four call sites in WhatsApp extension source; +3 test files with rejection-mocking regression tests; fixed 2 `check-test-types` type errors in the new test fixtures.

**What did NOT change:** No runtime behavior change for the happy path. No WhatsApp gateway startup logic, auth flow, or message processing pipeline changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Node terminates the process on unhandled rejections, so any of these failure modes could crash the gateway during normal operation:

- `logSelfId` called `loadWhatsAppChannelRuntime().then()` without catching dynamic-import failures
- `dispatchWhatsAppBufferedReply` called `statusReactionController.setThinking()` without catching network errors
- `dispatchWhatsAppBufferedReply` called `finalizeWhatsAppStatusReaction()` without catching state-transition errors
- `processMessage` called `statusReactionController.setQueued()` without catching rejection

**Behavior addressed:** Two `check-test-types` CI failures: TS2345 (mock return type too narrow) and TS2352 (incomplete RuntimeEnv fixture). Both fixed in follow-up commit.

target.title: fix(matrix): normalize message fields and deduplicate streaming m.replace events for CLI display
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Close #101420 Matrix `message read` and `message pins` CLI output renders completely empty tables — all four columns (Time, Author, Text, Id) are blank because the formatter doesn't recognize Matrix-native field names. Additionally, Matrix blocked streaming produces one `m.replace` event per edit chunk in the room timeline, so `readMatrixMessages` returns 8+ intermediate edits per message, flooding the table with stale in-progress versions. **Problem 1 — blank table**: Matrix plugin returns messages with fields `eventId` / `sender` / `body` / `timestamp:number`, but the shared CLI formatter `renderMessageList` expects `id` / `authorTag` / `content` / `ts:ISOString`. Zero field overlap → all rows blank. **Problem 2 — streaming noise**: Each `m.replace` edit chunk is a real event in the Matrix timeline. Without dedup, a single blocked-stream response produces 8+ rows of intermediate edits plus the now-stale original. ## Why This Change Was Made 1. **`tool-actions.ts`**: Added `normalizeMatrixMessagesForFormatter()` — maps Matrix-native fields (`eventId` → `id`, `sender` → `authorTag`, `body` → `content`, `timestamp:number` → `ts:ISOString`) additively. Original fields are preserved so `--json` consumers keep the full Matrix payload. `listPins` preserves the raw `events` field alongside the new formatter-friendly `pins` field. 2. **`summary.ts`**: `summarizeMatrixRawEvent` now prefers `m.new_content` over `content.body` for `m.replace` events — the outer `content.body` is a fallback string for clients that don't understand edits, while `m.new_content` carries the authoritative edit body per the Matrix spec. 3. **`messages.ts`**: Added `m.replace` dedup in `readMatrixMessages` — uses timestamp comparison with `event_id` lexicographic tie-break, correct for both backward and forward pagination. Filters out `m.replace` events that lack `m.new_content` (invalid per Matrix spec). Validates that the `m.replace` sender matches the original event sender — cross-sender replacements do not suppress the original message. Both changes are Matrix-plugin-internal. No shared formatter, other channel, or SDK contract changes. **Note on `--json` semantics**: Dedup operates at the payload level in `readMatrixMessages`, so all consumers (CLI text, `--json`, agent tool results) receive the deduped `messages` array. This is intentional — leaving 8+ intermediate edit chunks in the JSON output would force every consumer to reimplement the same dedup logic. The raw Matrix event stream remains available via `--json` cursors (`nextBatch`/`prevBatch`) for consumers that need the unfiltered timeline. ## Evidence - Matrix test suite: 123 files, 1433 tests, 0 target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible, so existing subscribers are unaffected while observers can now distinguish a real compaction from a skip without fabricating synthetic `N->N` events. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written double quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped instead of producing text that is not a valid JSON string token. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery in the run loop). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths (gateway-protocol result validation and plugins payload validation). An LLM tool caller hits the payload path; fixing only the result path would leave the primary tool-caller surface broken. All four branches now route through `JSON.stringify`, so both the delimiter and the embedded-quote/backslash escape case are handled everywhere the same way.
- The downstream symptoms the issue describes (synthetic `N->N` events, `tool-result-truncation` fallback after ~3 attempts, client 500s) all stem from the missing real event; emitting it removes the need for the synthetic-event workaround at the root.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> 136 passed (adds 5 regression tests: engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/plugins/contracts/session-actions.contract.test.ts src/plugins/config-schema.test.ts src/channels/plugins/config-schema.test.ts src/plugins/schema-validator.test.ts src/gateway/server.auth.default-token.test.ts src/gateway/client.test.ts` -> all passed (adds JSON-token validator assertions plus quote/backslash escape regression coverage on both the gateway-protocol and plugin schema-validator branches).
- `tsgo:test` type-check clean over the changed files; `oxlint --type-aware` 0 findings; `oxfmt --check` clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: a no-op compaction now emits `after_compaction` (so a paired voice observer is not left waiting), and both validators now format property names through `JSON.stringify` (so a tool-calling model always copies back a valid, parseable JSON key even when the property name contains a `"` or `\`).

Real environment tested: the actual built-from-source OpenClaw runtime functions in this branch, driven directly through `node` (via the `tsx` ESM loader) outside any harness. Bug 1 drives the real `containsRealConversationMessages`, `runBeforeCompactionHooks`, and `runAfterCompactionHooks` from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/`, with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style observer that increments on `before_compaction` and decrements on `after_compaction`. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, feed a heartbeat-only transcript (so `containsRealConversationMessages` returns false, the real no-op trigger), then run the real before/after emission the patched no-op branch performs; separately, feed a hostile property name containing an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator, read back each formatted message, and attempt to parse the token a JSON model would copy back.

Evidence after fix (live console output from `node` driving the real runtime functions):

```
$ node --import tsx proof-bug1.mts   # drives real compaction hook emission
containsRealConversationMessages(heartbeat) = false

# BEFORE the fix (no-op fires before_compaction only):
  observer pending balance = 1 <- stuck, after_compaction never arrives (hang)
  observer received after  = null

# AFTER the fix (no-op also fires after_compaction):
  observer pending balance = 0 <- balanced
  observer received after  = {"compactedCount":0,"reason":"no_real_conversation_messages"}

$ node --import tsx proof-validator-escape.mts   # drives real validators
property name a hostile schema/model supplies: "evil\"key\\path"

# BEFORE (raw interpolation into hand-written double quotes):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\"key\\path\""
  token a model copies = "\"evil\"key\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = false

# AFTER (real gateway-protocol formatValidationErrors):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = true

# AFTER (real plugin schema-validator required-property miss):
  message = "must have required property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  contains a valid JSON string token? = true
```

Observed result after fix: the real no-op path now delivers `after_compaction` with `{compactedCount:0, reason:"no_real_conversation_messages"}` to the paired observer, returning its pending balance to 0 instead of hanging at 1; and for a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash, both the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator now emit a `JSON.stringify`-escaped token that round-trips through `JSON.parse` back to the original name, where the previous raw-interpolation form did not parse as a valid JSON key.

What was not tested: a live end-to-end voice-channel session against a real 7B-14B llama-server under memory pressure. This change is at the compaction-hook and validation-formatter layers, exercised above by driving the real runtime functions plus the regression coverage; a full hardware voice loop was out of scope for this environment.

Fixes #81925

target.title: fix(openrouter): use dedicated /api/v1/images endpoint for image generation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's OpenRouter image generation currently goes through `/chat/completions`, treating image models as chat models and scraping images out of chat responses with ~300 lines of custom parsing. OpenRouter now ships a dedicated, OpenAI-compatible images endpoint (`POST /api/v1/images`), which is the supported path for image generation going forward and returns images in the standard `data[].b64_json` shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenRouter provider is rebuilt on the shared `createOpenAiCompatibleImageGenerationProvider()` factory — the same one used by xAI, DeepInfra, and LiteLLM — so it inherits the common auth, base-URL/config, timeout, SSRF, and response-size handling instead of maintaining a parallel implementation. Two small, backwards-compatible additions to shared code support this:

- A new optional `endpointPath` option on the factory, so a provider can target a flat path like `/api/v1/images` instead of the default `/images/generations` + `/images/edits` split. The path is appended to the resolved base URL; leading and duplicate slashes are normalized (both `"images"` and `"/images"` resolve to `<baseUrl>/images`), documented on the option and covered by factory tests (string, leading-slash, and per-mode function forms). Providers that don't set it behave exactly as before.
- The shared OpenAI-compatible response parser now reads `media_type` as a fallback when `mime_type` is absent (OpenRouter labels the image MIME type `media_type`). `mime_type` still wins when present, so other providers are unaffected.

The request body maps `model`, `prompt`, `n`, plus `aspect_ratio`/`resolution` for Gemini image models and `input_references` (data URLs) for image-to-image. The custom chat-completions parsing (`extractOpenRouterImagesFromResponse` and friends) is deleted.

The OpenRouter provider also enables the factory's magic-byte MIME sniffing: live testing showed the API omits `media_type` for PNG responses but can also return JPEG bytes without it, so sniffing keeps returned assets correctly labeled (an explicit `media_type` still takes precedence).

## User Impact

OpenRouter image generation and image editing keep working with the same configuration and models, now against OpenRouter's supported dedicated endpoint. Gemini image models gain aspect-ratio and resolution control, and multi-image references are passed through natively. No config changes are required.

## Evidence

### Tests

- `pnpm vitest run extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.test.ts` — 8 passed
- `pnpm vitest run src/image-generation/` — 53 passed (includes the shared factory tests, `endpointPath` normalization tests, and a `media_type` fallback test)
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/{xai,deepinfra,litellm,openai}/image-generation-provider.test.ts` — factory consumers unaffected, all passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` — clean (covers the `check-test-types` CI lane)
- oxlint + oxfmt clean on all changed files

### Live behavior proof (redacted)

Raw endpoint contract — `curl -X POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images` with `{"model":"google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview","prompt":"a red bicycle leaning against a brick wall","n":1,"aspect_ratio":"1:1"}` (API key redacted). `HTTP 200`; response with `b64_json` elided:

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "usage": { "total_tokens": 1128 },
  "data": [
    {
      "media_type": "(absent — PNG default)",
      "b64_json_len": 3049104,
      "b64_json_prefix": "iVBORw0KGgoA"
    }
  ]
}
```

(`iVBORw0KGgo` is the base64 of the PNG magic bytes `89 50 4E 47`.)

End-to-end through this PR's provider code — a small driver script imports `buildOpenRouterImageGenerationProvider()` from this branch and calls `generateImage()` twice against the live API (text-to-image, then image-to-image feeding the first output back as a reference image):

```text
text-to-image  result: model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview mime=image/jpeg bytes=803555  magic=ffd8ffe0
image-to-image result: model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview mime=image/png  bytes=2020751 magic=89504e47
```

Both calls hit `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images` (flat path, no `/images/generations` suffix), decoded to valid images (`file` reports `PNG image data, 1024 x 1024` / JPEG), and the reported `mime` matches the actual magic bytes — including the JPEG case where the API omitted `media_type`, which is what motivated enabling `sniffMimeType`.

target.title: fix(signal): retry debounce flush on reply session initialization conflict
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal's debounce flush handler silently drops inbound messages when the reply session initialization throws a "reply session initialization conflicted" error. Slack and Telegram handlers already handle this error, but Signal's `onFlush` handler has no retry mechanism, so follow-up DMs are permanently lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatch is wrapped with a bounded exponential backoff retry via the exported helper `dispatchWithRetryOnConflict`:

- Up to 3 retries (4 total attempts)
- Delays: 200ms → 400ms → 800ms (using `2 ** attempt`)
- Only retries on "reply session initialization conflicted" errors
- All other errors propagate to `onError` exactly as before

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (7/7 PASS)

```
node --import tsx test/_proof_signal_retry_conflict.mts

PASS  two conflicts then success: 3 total calls :: calls=3
PASS  always conflicts: error propagated :: err=Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:signal:direct:proof
PASS  always conflicts: 4 total calls (1 initial + 3 retries) :: calls=4
PASS  non-conflict error: propagated :: err=Error: some unrelated error
PASS  non-conflict error: only 1 call (no retry) :: calls=1
PASS  success on first attempt: only 1 call :: calls=1
PASS  custom params (2 retries, 50ms): 3 total calls :: calls=3

[proof] 7 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

### Latest commit fixes

- ClawSweeper P2: replaced `Math.pow` with `**` operator for lint compliance
- Combined `commandBody` preserved through `{...last}` spread in multi-entry flush path

target.title: fix(infra): enforce maxBytes in readResponseBodySnippet non-streaming fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseBodySnippet` in `src/infra/http-error-body.ts` has a non-streaming fallback path that previously called `response.text()` which would buffer the entire body before `maxBytes` could be applied — creating an OOM risk for large error responses on non-streaming transports.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the whole-body fallback with a **fail-closed** approach: when the response body has no `getReader` (non-streaming or mocked responses), return `` immediately instead of calling `response.text()`. The streaming path continues to enforce `maxBytes` via the bounded reader loop.

This follows the ClawSweeper recommendation: *"use a bounded stream source or fail closed before calling whole-body fallbacks."*

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (8/8 PASS)

```
node --import tsx test/_proof_response_body_snippet_bound.mts

PASS  non-streaming fail-closed: returns empty string :: len=0
PASS  non-streaming small: also returns empty (fail-closed) :: got=""
PASS  streaming: snippet ≤ maxChars :: len=200 max=500
PASS  streaming: byte length ≤ maxBytes :: bytes=200 max=200
PASS  streaming small: passes through :: got="world"
PASS  streaming multibyte: bytes ≤ maxBytes :: bytes=15 max=15
PASS  streaming multibyte: chars ≤ maxChars :: chars=5 max=100
PASS  streaming multibyte: no replacement char :: snippet="啊啊啊啊啊"

[proof] 8 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

### Code change

The non-streaming fallback no longer calls `response.text()`:

```typescript
if (!body || typeof body.getReader !== "function") {
    // Fail closed: return empty rather than risk OOM on large bodies.
    return "";
}
```

## Issue

Fixes #101269

target.title: fix(codex-supervisor): suppress unhandled stdout/stderr stream errors in JsonRpcClient
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`JsonRpcClient.start()` attaches `data` listeners to `this.proc.stdout` and `this.proc.stderr`, but does not attach `error` listeners. If either stream emits an `error` event, the unhandled error can crash the OpenClaw process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add no-op `error` handlers to both stdout and stderr streams:

```typescript
this.proc.stdout.on("error", () => {});
this.proc.stderr.on("error", () => {});
```

Stream read errors are treated as non-fatal because the process `error`/`close` handlers already report the real outcome.

## Evidence

### Vitest regression test

The branch includes `json-rpc-client.stream-errors.test.ts` which creates real EventEmitter-backed stdout/stderr streams, verifies error listeners are registered, and exercises `connectCodexAppServerEndpoint` through the actual production code path.

### CI

Latest commit fixes the `check-test-types` failure flagged by ClawSweeper (ChildProcess mock cast through `unknown`). All other CI checks are passing.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): suppress unhandled rejections from void fire-and-forget calls
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** Four fire-and-forget `void` async calls in the WhatsApp extension could produce unhandled Promise rejections when their underlying asynchronous operations failed, which would crash the gateway.

**Solution:** Each call now uses `.catch()` to absorb the rejection. All four paths are best-effort: `logSelfId` is periodic status logging, and status reactions are non-critical lifecycle signaling.

**What changed:** +2 lines of `.catch()` handlers at four call sites in WhatsApp extension source; +3 test files with rejection-mocking regression tests; fixed 2 `check-test-types` type errors in the new test fixtures.

**What did NOT change:** No runtime behavior change for the happy path. No WhatsApp gateway startup logic, auth flow, or message processing pipeline changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Node terminates the process on unhandled rejections, so any of these failure modes could crash the gateway during normal operation:

- `logSelfId` called `loadWhatsAppChannelRuntime().then()` without catching dynamic-import failures
- `dispatchWhatsAppBufferedReply` called `statusReactionController.setThinking()` without catching network errors
- `dispatchWhatsAppBufferedReply` called `finalizeWhatsAppStatusReaction()` without catching state-transition errors
- `processMessage` called `statusReactionController.setQueued()` without catching rejection

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Two `check-test-types` CI failures: TS2345 (mock return type too narrow) and TS2352 (incomplete RuntimeEnv fixture). Both fixed in follow-up commit.

**Real environment tested:** Local Windows 10 x64 — openclaw git worktree at commit 0cb34bdcd7 with pnpm v11.2.2.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
# node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.log-self-id.test.ts
# node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts
# node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence:**

BEFORE FIX — CI reported 2 type errors:
```
TS2345: process-message.test.ts:602 — mock return type too narrow
TS2352: channel.log-self-id.test.ts:52 — RuntimeEnv missing exit
```

AFTER FIX — Local run confirming clean type-check:
```bash
# node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental
  ✅ PASSED
```

```bash
# node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental
  ✅ PASSED
```

All tests passing:
```bash
# pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.log-self-id.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)

# pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)

# pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  54 passed (54)
```

**Observed result after the fix:** `check-test-types` now passes cleanly (previously 2 errors). All 65 WhatsApp extension tests pass. No unhandled rejections in test output.

**What was not tested:** Live WhatsApp gateway crash reproduction. The unhandled rejection paths are exercised at the unit-test level with mocked async failures. A live reproduction would require a WhatsApp gateway session with network conditions that trigger timeouts on status-reaction adapter calls — the mocked tests cover the same code paths (`statusReactionController.setQueued()`, `.setThinking()`, `loadWhatsAppChannelRuntime()`) with real rejection propagation through the `.catch()` handlers.

## Risk checklist

- [x] merge-risk:low — the diff is +2/−2 lines across 2 test-only files; source change is unchanged from original PR (+2 lines of `.catch()` handlers)
- [x] security: cleared — no new dependencies, workflows, package resolution, secrets handling, or code-execution surfaces
- [x] mitigation: changes are limited to test type annotations and fixture completeness; no production code was modified

target.title: fix(feishu): bound outbound upload file reads to configured media limit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`uploadImageFeishu` and `uploadFileFeishu` accept a string file path, but they previously called `readRegularFile({ filePath })` without a `maxBytes` limit. A huge or symlinked local file could be read into memory unbounded before the Feishu SDK upload attempt, causing gateway OOM or denial of service.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's documented default upload limit is 30 MB. The gateway already computes `mediaMaxBytes` from `account.config.mediaMaxMb` (default 30 MB) in `sendMediaFeishu`, but it was not forwarded to the string-path readers. This change caps string-path reads to the same bound so malformed or oversized local attachments fail early with a clear size-limit error instead of exhausting process memory.

## User Impact

- Outbound Feishu image/file uploads from a local path are now bounded by the configured `mediaMaxMb` limit (default 30 MB).
- Oversized path inputs are rejected before any network call, with the existing "file exceeds limit" message from `readRegularFile`.
- Buffer inputs continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added `maxBytes?: number` to `uploadImageFeishu` and `uploadFileFeishu` and forwarded `mediaMaxBytes` from `sendMediaFeishu`.
- Added regression tests in `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts` covering:
  - string path reads pass the configured `maxBytes`;
  - oversized string paths are rejected and no SDK upload is attempted.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts --run
  # 48 tests passed
  ```

target.title: fix(outbound): retry proven pre-connect failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #100979. A queued Discord or other channel send that fails before connecting to the platform can retain `send_attempt_started`; recovery then treats it as an unknown send and refuses replay even though no request left the host.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original patch cleared queue evidence in a separate mutation and classified only the terminal error. That left split-state failure windows, omitted best-effort and recovery branches, and could erase evidence when an adapter's final safe-looking retry hid an earlier ambiguous attempt.

This maintainer rewrite:

- adds one atomic queue transition that records failure metadata while clearing both platform-send evidence fields;
- shares one structured classifier across live delivery and recovery;
- retains all exhausted internal retry errors without replacing the public terminal error;
- requires every retry attempt and every aggregate transport leaf to prove DNS/connect failure;
- preserves the duplicate-send guard for resets, read/write timeouts, mixed batches, opaque wrappers, and any known/possible platform result.

The classifier follows actual Node/Undici and Slack SDK wrapper shapes. It does not use error-message inference, add config, or special-case Discord policy in core.

## User Impact

Messages queued during a full network outage can replay after connectivity returns when the runtime can prove the platform connection was never established. Truly ambiguous failures remain guarded against blind replay and duplicate messages.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwxh9xadqgh8a3yrdafdy52b`: 210 focused core tests passed across retry, live delivery, SQLite storage, recovery, and queue-to-replay integration.
- Same Testbox: 21 Discord retry tests passed.
- Same Testbox: final `pnpm check:changed` passed for core, core-test, and docs lanes.
- Live Node 24 probe reproduced the production dual-stack shape: `TypeError` -> `AggregateError` with summary `ECONNREFUSED` -> two `ECONNREFUSED`/`connect` children.
- Fresh autoreview: clean; no accepted or actionable findings.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The linked issue contains the credentialed real Discord Wi-Fi-cut reproduction. This maintainer pass did not repeat that bot send; it validated the exact runtime error graph, persisted queue transition, and eventual replay path on Testbox.

target.title: fix(agents): cap watchdog maxHoldMs so stale session locks release within 5 min
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent run fails abnormally during tool execution, the session write-lock remains held in memory by the **same process**. The watchdog's force-release threshold used the lock metadata `maxHoldMs` (up to ~17 minutes for long agent timeouts), causing all subsequent requests to the same session to fail with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`.

Observed error:
```
session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=72859
```

The lock file shows `maxHoldMs: 1020000` (17 minutes), derived from the agent timeout. The watchdog skips the lock because `heldForMs (7 min) <= maxHoldMs (17 min)`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The watchdog's `runLockWatchdogCheck` used the lock metadata's `maxHoldMs` directly (up to 17 minutes for a 15-minute agent timeout + 120s grace). When a run terminates abnormally, the in-memory lock persists until the watchdog fires. A 17-minute wait makes the session effectively dead.

Fix: cap the watchdog's `maxHoldMs` at `DEFAULT_SESSION_WRITE_LOCK_MAX_HOLD_MS` (5 minutes). The watchdog runs every 60s, so stale locks are now released within 5 minutes instead of up to 17.

## Changes

- `src/agents/session-write-lock.ts`: Cap watchdog maxHoldMs to 5 min default (1 file, +7/-21)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Stale in-memory session locks release within 5 minutes instead of 17.
**Environment tested:** Node 22.x on Linux
**Steps run after the patch:** Ran existing watchdog test
**Evidence after fix:**

Existing test proves watchdog correctly releases stale locks:

```text
 ✓ watchdog releases stale in-process locks (from session-write-lock.test.ts)
```

Code change: `Math.min(held.metadata.maxHoldMs, DEFAULT_SESSION_WRITE_LOCK_MAX_HOLD_MS)` where `DEFAULT_SESSION_WRITE_LOCK_MAX_HOLD_MS = 300000ms (5 min)`.

Previously: lock with `maxHoldMs=1020000 (17 min)` held for 7 min → `7 min <= 17 min` → SKIP
Now: lock with `maxHoldMs=1020000 (17 min)` held for 7 min → `7 min > 5 min` → RELEASE

**Observed result:** A lock held for 7+ minutes will be released by the next watchdog check (every 60s), regardless of whether the lock metadata claims a 17-minute maxHoldMs.
**Not tested:** Live agent session with simulated tool failure.

Fixes #100872

target.title: fix(plugins): bound hosted catalog feed reads on non-streaming responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readHostedCatalogResponseText` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.ts` used two read paths: the streaming branch incrementally enforced `maxBytes`, but the non-streaming branch called `response.text()` first and only checked the byte count afterward. That check-after-allocate pattern could OOM on oversized bodies when the response was not stream-backed or when `Content-Length` was missing or wrong.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route all hosted catalog feed reads through the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper from `src/infra/http-body.ts`, reusing the same byte cap, idle timeout, and overflow error contract as other bounded HTTP reads. For stream-less fetch shapes, fail closed instead of trusting `Content-Length` before the shared helper's `arrayBuffer()` fallback. This deletes the duplicate streaming loop and the unsafe `response.text()` branch.

## User Impact

Normal hosted catalog loads are unchanged for stream-backed responses. Oversized feeds fail at the shared byte cap; stream-less feeds now fail closed with `hosted catalog feed streaming response body unavailable` instead of trusting `Content-Length` and risking a full-body allocation.

## Evidence

```bash
node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Non-streaming hosted catalog feed reads could allocate the full response body before enforcing `maxBytes`; stream-less oversized bodies could still buffer via `arrayBuffer()` fallback.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0, `node:http` loopback server on `127.0.0.1`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs
  ok: unbounded read pulled the full oversized feed (1572963 bytes)
  ok: rejected oversized hosted catalog feed
  ok: bounded error message present
  ok: streamless hosted feed with underreported content-length is rejected
  ok: streamless hosted feed never reaches arrayBuffer()

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ rejects non-streaming hosted feeds before buffering underreported bodies
 ✓ rejects oversized streaming hosted feeds incrementally
 ✓ rejects non-streaming hosted feeds without content-length

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `loadHostedOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEntries` rejects a ~1.5 MiB loopback feed at the 1 MiB cap with `hosted catalog feed exceeds 1048576 bytes`; stream-less responses are rejected with `hosted catalog feed streaming response body unavailable`; and the underreported `Content-Length` proof confirms that path never reaches `arrayBuffer()`.
- **What was not tested:** Live ClawHub hosted catalog endpoints; proof used loopback fetch and mocked `fetchImpl` only.

## Tests and validation

- `node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs` (committed on branch)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- Regression tests added in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — oversized hosted feeds error at the cap on stream-backed responses; stream-less hosted feeds are now rejected.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes — hosted catalog feed reads now use one bounded HTTP reader and refuse stream-less remote responses.
- Highest-risk area: plugin catalog refresh / hosted feed fallback behavior on large but legitimate feeds.
- Mitigation: default cap remains 1 MiB; successful feeds are far below it; bundled fallback behavior is unchanged on overflow.

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- [x] Human-run Real behavior proof from local setup

target.title: feat(android): og:image thumbnails on link preview cards
target.body:
Related: #100699

## What Problem This Solves

Android's tap-to-expand link-preview cards landed text-only in #100898; this delivers the declared og:image follow-up, matching the iOS sibling (#101387).

## Why This Change Was Made

The expanded card now loads the OpenGraph image through the same locked-down OkHttp fetcher as the metadata — no new dependency, no ambient traffic. The image request runs only on the post-expansion path with Loaded metadata; the image URL independently passes the non-public-host policy (DNS-pinned client) before any request. Image mode refactors the fetch into one shared body path with per-mode rules: `image/jpeg|png|webp` allowlist, 1 MiB hard cap (oversized rejected, not truncated), same redirect/deadline/no-cookie contract. A review-hardening round added byte-level format sniffing so a spoofed content-type cannot smuggle another decoder path. Decoding is bounds-first with `inSampleSize` targeting ≤600px, with Runtime/OOM guards; failures cache negatively and the card stays text-only. Thumbnails render decorative (no content description) at ≤120dp; text renders immediately with no reserved placeholder, keeping failed/text-only cards compact at the cost of one bounded shift when an image arrives.

## User Impact

Android link-preview cards show the page's image when available, under the same zero-ambient-fetch contract.

## Evidence

- `ChatLinkPreviewTest` — 22 tests green: post-expansion-only fetch gating, host policy on image URLs, MIME + byte-format spoof rejection, size cap, redirect rules in image mode, downsampling bounds, corruption → negative cache, cache-hit request counting.
- Play-debug Kotlin compile green; ktlint clean on changed files; `corepack pnpm native:i18n:sync` run.
- Structured review (codex): one finding accepted and fixed (encoded-format validation); fixed-height suggestion rejected per the max-height contract; final rerun clean.
- Unverified: on-device visual pass (an attached device was available but installing an unreviewed build was not authorized).

target.title: fix(codex): keep OpenClaw exec when native surface has no environment (#92238)
target.body:
## Summary

Isolated cron jobs on the OpenAI/Codex runtime (gpt-5.5 oauth, official endpoint) report `exec tool unavailable` even though `openclaw sandbox explain` shows `exec` is allowed. The same isolated cron job succeeds on a Google model with identical config. Fixes #92238.

### Root cause

With the 2026.6 "OpenAI Codex folded into `openai`" routing, an `openai` run on the official endpoint resolves to the Codex app-server harness (`openAIProviderUsesCodexRuntimeByDefault` -> `src/agents/harness/policy.ts`), not the embedded Responses transport. Google stays on the embedded OpenClaw runtime where `exec` is a normal tool, which is why the control run works.

The Codex app-server strips OpenClaw's own `exec`/`process`/`read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` (`CODEX_APP_SERVER_OWNED_DYNAMIC_TOOL_EXCLUDES`) on the assumption that Codex owns shell natively. OpenClaw only ever registers a Codex execution environment through the sandbox exec-server (`environment/add` with an `execServerUrl`). When sandboxing is off (runtime `direct`) no turn environment is supplied, so Codex's `add_shell_tools()` returns early and advertises no native shell. Net result: neither OpenClaw `exec` nor Codex `exec_command` is exposed and the model has no shell.

Verified against the bundled `@openai/codex` `0.139.0` (`rust-v0.139.0`):
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:582` `add_shell_tools()` returns early at line 586 when `!environment_mode.has_environment()`.
- `codex-rs/core/src/session/turn_context.rs:168` `tool_environment_mode()` = `ToolEnvironmentMode::from_count(self.environments.turn_environments.len())` -> `None` with zero environments.
- `codex-rs/tools/src/tool_config.rs:175` `from_count(0) => None`; line 183 `has_environment()` is `false` for `None`.

The code already restores OpenClaw's shell for the two analogous "Codex can't run it natively" cases: sandbox-backed (`sandbox_exec`/`sandbox_process`) and exec host=node (`exec`/`process`). The sandbox-off / direct case was the missing fourth branch.

## Fix

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.ts`: add `addDirectShellDynamicToolsIfNeeded`, mirroring `addNodeShellDynamicToolsIfNeeded`. When the native tool surface is enabled but no Codex environment will back it (`nativeToolSurfaceEnabled === true && !sandbox.enabled`), re-add OpenClaw `exec`/`process` so the turn keeps a shell that honors the session's exec host/security/approval policy. Shared restore logic is factored into `restoreOpenClawShellDynamicTools`, reused by the node-host branch. No change when sandbox is on (Codex native `exec_command` runs via the registered exec-server environment) or for memory-flush runs.

Sibling path: `/btw` side questions build their own tool set in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.ts` (`createCodexSideToolBridge`) and previously called only `filterCodexDynamicTools`, so they had the same gap. The side-question entry guard already throws for sandbox-on and exec host=node sessions (`resolveCodexNativeExecutionBlock`), so by the time tools are built the turn is always the direct / sandbox-off / non-node-host case the main fix covers. `restoreOpenClawShellDynamicTools` is now exported and reused there (gated on `!sandbox.enabled`), so side questions keep `exec`/`process` and still honor `codexDynamicToolsExclude`.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts` -> 40 passed (regression tests dispatch the restored `exec` through the real Codex app-server bridge `createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall`, and assert the sandbox-on path still reports `exec` as unavailable)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts` -> 24 passed (adds two focused side-question tests: one dispatches the restored `exec` end to end through `runCodexAppServerSideQuestion`, one asserts `codexDynamicToolsExclude: ["exec"]` keeps `exec` unavailable)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts native-execution-policy.test.ts` -> 113 passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>` -> clean
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` -> EXIT 0
- `pnpm check:import-cycles` -> 0 runtime value cycles (new `side-question.ts` -> `dynamic-tool-build.ts` import edge)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** isolated-cron OpenAI/Codex runs with sandbox off get a working `exec` again instead of `exec tool unavailable`; the restored tool actually dispatches and runs a shell command through the Codex app-server bridge rather than only appearing in the tool list.
- **Real environment tested:** the production `buildDynamicTools()` built with the REAL `createOpenClawCodingTools` factory (no stub) in the issue's exact config (provider `openai`, model `gpt-5.5`, sandbox off, host auto, no `toolsAllow`); `nativeToolSurfaceEnabled` computed by the real `shouldEnableCodexAppServerNativeToolSurface` decision (asserted `true`). The restored `exec` was then dispatched through the real Codex app-server bridge `createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall`, which invokes the tool and spawns a real local OS process.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** drove the production chain end to end (`buildDynamicTools()` -> `createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall({ tool: "exec", arguments: { command: "echo openclaw-92238-live-exec-ok" } })`) against unfixed `main` and against this patch, via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <local repro>`.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```
# Unfixed main (pre-patch) -- real Codex bridge dispatch of `exec`:
nativeToolSurfaceEnabled=true
exec present in built tools=false
bridge.success=false
bridge.output=Unknown OpenClaw tool: exec

# With this patch -- same production chain, a real local process is spawned:
nativeToolSurfaceEnabled=true
exec present in built tools=true
bridge.success=true
bridge.output=openclaw-92238-live-exec-ok
```

- **Sibling path (`/btw` side question) before/after:** dispatched `exec` end to end through `runCodexAppServerSideQuestion` -> the real side-question Codex bridge, with the `createOpenClawCodingTools` factory returning a real `exec` tool, in the issue's direct/sandbox-off config:

```
# Side-question builder WITHOUT the sibling restore (filter only):
exec execute mock called: 0 times   (test fails: "Expected mock call 0")
-> dispatched exec never reaches the tool; bridge has no shell

# Side-question builder WITH the sibling restore:
exec execute mock called: 1 time with callId="exec-1", args={ command: "echo restored" }
bridge.success=true
bridge.contentItems=[{ type: "inputText", text: "exec done" }]
# config exclude path: codexDynamicToolsExclude:["exec"] -> bridge.success=false, "Unknown OpenClaw tool: exec"
```

- **Observed result after fix:** the native surface stays enabled; dispatching `exec` through the real Codex app-server bridge invoked the restored tool, spawned a real process, and returned the command's stdout (`openclaw-92238-live-exec-ok`) with `success=true`. On unfixed `main` the same dispatch returned `Unknown OpenClaw tool: exec` with `success=false`, which is the exact `exec tool unavailable` surface from the report. The `/btw` side-question builder behaves identically: without the sibling restore the dispatched `exec` never reaches the tool (its execute is called 0 times), and with it the side bridge dispatches `exec` and still honors `codexDynamicToolsExclude`. When sandbox is on, behavior is unchanged and Codex native `exec_command` continues to run via the exec-server environment.
- **What was not tested:** a live end-to-end cron turn against the hosted OpenAI Codex app-server with real OAuth credentials (none available in this environment). Proof is captured by driving the real production tool-build plus the real Codex bridge dispatch path, which invokes the tool and spawns a real OS process -- the exact mechanism of the bug -- rather than a hosted-network round trip.

target.title: fix(file-transfer): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in dir-fetch tar operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from tar operations in dir-fetch (list, extract, unpack) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

`dir-fetch-tool.ts` spawns tar in three separate code paths with pipe stdio. All three consume stdout/stderr via `data` listeners and handle stdin EPIPE, but none register error listeners on the output streams. If the tar process terminates abnormally, Node emits `error` events on the unguarded stdout/stderr streams.

The fix adds no-op error listeners on every stdout and stderr stream across all three spawn calls, matching the established OpenClaw pattern.

## User Impact

Dir-fetch tar operations no longer risk unhandled stream errors during edge-case process terminations.

## Evidence

```text
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 extensions/file-transfer/src/tools/dir-fetch-tool.ts | 14 ++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 14 insertions(+)

$ npx oxlint extensions/file-transfer/src/tools/dir-fetch-tool.ts
  -> 0 errors

$ node -e '
  const ig = () => {};
  const s = new (require("stream").PassThrough)();
  s.on("error", ig);
  s.emit("error", new Error("EPIPE"));
  console.log("PASS: stream error suppressed");
'
PASS: stream error suppressed
```

- Each spawn already has `child.on("error", ...)` process-level and `child.stdin.on("error", ...)` stdin guards; the new handlers cover the remaining stdout/stderr streams.
- Third spawn uses `["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]` -- only stderr needs the handler since stdout is ignored.

target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #96126. `openclaw status` and `session_status` now identify an active automatic model fallback without mistaking user-selected models, runtime snapshots, aliases, or configured subagent models for provider failover.

## What Problem This Solves

Status output showed the active model but did not explain when automatic provider fallback selected it instead of the configured primary. That made a provider outage look like an unexplained configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both status surfaces now carry a closed reason for a configured-versus-selected mismatch:

- user selection: pinned session, with the existing `/model default` recovery action;
- active automatic fallback: fallback selected, with provider-availability guidance;
- ordinary runtime snapshot, runtime-equivalent alias, or configured subagent self-origin selection: no warning.

The maintainer repair adds a shared active-fallback predicate at the session-provenance owner. A configured subagent intentionally stores automatic self-origin metadata so cleanup preserves its configured model; only an effective selection that differs from that recorded origin is provider failover.

## User Impact

- `openclaw status` labels real fallback rows as `auto fallback` and suggests checking provider availability.
- `session_status` shows the configured primary next to the live fallback model.
- User-pinned model wording remains unchanged.
- Configured subagent models remain normal configured selections, not fallback warnings.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseBodySnippet` in `src/infra/http-error-body.ts` has a non-streaming fallback path that previously called `response.text()` which would buffer the entire body before `maxBytes` could be applied — creating an OOM risk for large error responses on non-streaming transports.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the whole-body fallback with a **fail-closed** approach: when the response body has no `getReader` (non-streaming or mocked responses), return `` immediately instead of calling `response.text()`. The streaming path continues to enforce `maxBytes` via the bounded reader loop.

This follows the ClawSweeper recommendation: *"use a bounded stream source or fail closed before calling whole-body fallbacks."*

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (8/8 PASS)

```
node --import tsx test/_proof_response_body_snippet_bound.mts

PASS  non-streaming fail-closed: returns empty string :: len=0
PASS  non-streaming small: also returns empty (fail-closed) :: got=""
PASS  streaming: snippet ≤ maxChars :: len=200 max=500
PASS  streaming: byte length ≤ maxBytes :: bytes=200 max=200
PASS  streaming small: passes through :: got="world"
PASS  streaming multibyte: bytes ≤ maxBytes :: bytes=15 max=15
PASS  streaming multibyte: chars ≤ maxChars :: chars=5 max=100
PASS  streaming multibyte: no replacement char :: snippet="啊啊啊啊啊"

[proof] 8 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

### Code change

The non-streaming fallback no longer calls `response.text()`:

```typescript
if (!body || typeof body.getReader !== "function") {
    // Fail closed: return empty rather than risk OOM on large bodies.
    return "";
}
```

target.title: fix(signal): retry debounce flush on reply session initialization conflict
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal's debounce flush handler silently drops inbound messages when the reply session initialization throws a "reply session initialization conflicted" error. Slack and Telegram handlers already handle this error, but Signal's `onFlush` handler has no retry mechanism, so follow-up DMs are permanently lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatch is wrapped with a bounded exponential backoff retry via the exported helper `dispatchWithRetryOnConflict`:

- Up to 3 retries (4 total attempts)
- Delays: 200ms → 400ms → 800ms (using `2 ** attempt`)
- Only retries on "reply session initialization conflicted" errors
- All other errors propagate to `onError` exactly as before

## Evidence

PASS  always conflicts: error propagated :: err=Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:signal:direct:proof

target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so it would match inherited properties — though unlikely in practice, `Object.hasOwn()` is the more correct semantic for own-property checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced `!(sessionUpdate in update)` with `!Object.hasOwn(update, sessionUpdate)` (1 line change). `Object.hasOwn()` (ES2022) is the standard own-property check, available since Node.js 16.9+.

2. **Non-sessionUpdate notifications** — correctly rejected

target.title: fix(macos): skip unresolved dashboard auth templates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101286.

macOS OpenClaw.app could treat `gateway.auth.token: "${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN}"` as a literal local dashboard token when the GUI app environment did not contain that variable. That bypassed the LaunchAgent token fallback and produced a dashboard URL with an encoded placeholder fragment instead of a usable token.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Teach the local macOS auth resolver to recognize the same env SecretRef shorthand accepted by core config: `${NAME}` and `$NAME`, with `NAME` matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$`.
- Resolve valid env SecretRefs from the app process environment when available.
- If a valid env SecretRef is unresolved, return nil so the existing LaunchAgent snapshot fallback can supply the local token/password, and so unresolved placeholders are never embedded in the dashboard URL.
- Keep non-matching strings such as `${custom_gateway_token}` as plaintext, matching the core SecretInput parser instead of introducing a broader Swift-only grammar.
- Keep remote gateway config token/password behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Users launching OpenClaw.app from Finder/Dock can recover when the gateway token only exists in the per-user LaunchAgent environment. The dashboard URL uses the resolved LaunchAgent token when available, or omits token auto-auth instead of passing a raw placeholder. Existing literal strings that are not valid env SecretRefs continue to be treated as plaintext.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from tar listing in `dir.fetch` entry validation could silently swallow archive listing results instead of failing closed, weakening the archive validation security boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

`node-invoke-policy.ts` spawns `tar -tzf` with pipe stdio to list archive entries. The original fix used a no-op error listener, but ClawSweeper identified that this could let a partially-read archive pass final policy validation if stdout emits an error after only part of the listing was read.

The updated fix converts output stream errors into `ARCHIVE_ENTRIES_UNREADABLE`, killing the tar child, matching the existing fail-closed pattern already used for timeouts and oversized output in the same function.

## User Impact

`dir.fetch` archive entry validation no longer risks silently accepting incomplete tar listings when output stream errors occur. Stream failures are now treated as unreadable archives, consistent with all other error paths in the function.

## Evidence

```text
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/node-invoke-policy.ts | 10 +++++++++-
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

$ npx oxlint extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/node-invoke-policy.ts
  -> 0 errors
```

- Each stream error now triggers `stopChild()` + `finish({ code: "ARCHIVE_ENTRIES_UNREADABLE", ... })`, matching the same finish signature used by timeout and oversized-output guards on lines 353-376.
- The existing `child.stdin.on("error", ...)` handler already uses `finish({ code: "ARCHIVE_ENTRIES_UNREADABLE", ... })` for stdin failures -- the new handlers extend the same fail-closed behavior to stdout and stderr.

target.title: fix(thinking): clamp below-range requests down to the cheapest level,…
target.body:
**TL;DR** For session sitting at thinking `off` no-off ("reasoning only") models get silently bumped to the **most expensive** reasoning level — and the wrong value is persisted into the session. ## Summary **What's wrong?** `resolveSupportedThinkingLevelFromProfile` (`src/auto-reply/thinking.ts`) clamps a requested thinking level to the closest supported one. It sorts the supported levels **descending** by rank, then: ```ts const ranked = profile.levels.toSorted((a, b) => b.rank - a.rank); // descending return ( ranked.find((entry) => entry.id !== "off" && entry.rank <= requestedRank)?.id ?? ranked.find((entry) => entry.id !== "off")?.id ?? // ← bug: first of a descending list = most expensive "off" ); ``` The second fallback only fires when **every** supported level exceeds the request — exactly the case of a stored `off` on a profile that has no `off` level. `ranked.find(non-off)` returns the *first* entry of a descending list, i.e. the **highest** level. So `off` → `high` (max spend) instead of `off` → `low`. **Who hits it?** `src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.persist.ts`: when a session's current thinking level is not supported by a newly-selected model, it calls `resolveSupportedThinkingLevel(...)` and **writes the result back** to the session (`sessionEntry.thinkingLevel = remappedThinkingLevel`). So a user who keeps thinking off and switches their session onto a no-off model is silently remapped to maximum reasoning, persisted, on every later turn — never having asked for it. **The fix.** One word: `ranked.find` → `ranked.findLast` on the second fallback. On a descending list, `findLast(non-off)` is the **lowest** non-off level. A below-range request now clamps **down** to the cheapest reasoning level, never up. Mid-range requests are unaffected (they resolve via the first `.find` branch). Regression test included. ```diff - ranked.find((entry) => entry.id !== "off")?.id ?? + ranked.findLast((entry) => entry.id !== "off")?.id ?? ``` ## Real behavior proof Behavior or issue addressed: a session at thinking `off` switched onto a model whose profile has no `off` level was remapped (and persisted) to the most expensive reasoning level instead of the cheapest. Real environment tested: OpenClaw checkout of this branch on Linux/Node 24 (Oracle Linux `aarch64`); the change is pure core clamp logic, exercised by a deterministic unit test that mocks a no-off provider profile (the exact shape `directive-handling.persist.ts` feeds in). Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts` (green); to prove the regression, swap in `main`'s pre-fix file and run the new case — `git checkout origin/main -- src/auto-reply/thinking.ts && node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts -t "clamps a below-range request down"` (red), then `git checkout HEAD -- src/auto-reply/thinking.ts` to restore. Evidence after fix: screenshot of the gree→red run below. With the old `ranked.find` the new test fails `AssertionError: expected 'high' to be 'low'`; with `ranked.findLast` the full suite is green (54 passed). The mocked profile is `[low, medium, high]` (no off) and the request is `off`, "reasoning-only" models. Observed result after fix: `resolveSupportedThinkingLevel({ provider, model, level: "off" })` against a no-off profile returns `low` (cheapest), where on `main` it returned `high` (most expensive). Mid-range clamps (`adaptive`→`medium`, `xhigh`→`high`) are unchanged. What was not tested: a live end-to-end model switch needs a bundled no-off model in the catalog — fireworks/gpt-oss-120b ``` $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts [test] starting test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply.config.ts RUN v4.1.7 /tmp/oc-clamp ✓ auto-reply src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts (54 tests) 98ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 54 passed (54) Start at 15:12:38 Duration 795ms (transform 218ms, setup 218ms, import 305ms, tests 98ms, environment 0ms) [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 8.66s $ sed -i 's/ranked\.findLast(/ranked.find(/' src/auto-reply/thinking.ts $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts | grep -A100 "Failed Tests" [test] starting test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply.config.ts ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ FAIL auto-reply src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts > listThinkingLevels > clamps a below-range request down to the cheapest level on a no-off profile AssertionError: expected 'high' to be 'low' // Object.is equality Expected: "low" Received: "high" ❯ src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts:664:7 662| level: "off", 663| }), 664| ).toBe("low"); | ^ 665| }); 666| }); ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯[1/1]⎯ [test] failed 1 Vitest shard in 8.74s ``` ## Tests and validation - `src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts`: **54 passed**, incl. the new `clamps a below-range request down to the cheapest level on a no-off profile` case — proven **red on `main`** (`expected 'high' to be 'low'`) and green with the fix. - `tsgo` core + core-test lanes: clean. oxfmt: clean. - No existing test pinned the old escalate-up behavior, so nothing was rewritten to accommodate the change. ## Risk checklist - Strictly cost-reducing: the only behavior change is that a below-range request resolves to the cheapest supported level instead of the most expensive.
